Book - D&D Dragon of Icespire Peak

text.frame: “The Stonehill Inn is a modest, two-story roadhouse with the warm smell of stew and wood smoke drifting from its common room. The floorboards creak under the weight of weary travelers, and lantern light flickers across the walls. Laughter and whispers mix with the clink of mugs, though tonight, the air carries unease after the dragon’s roar. A friendly, broad-shouldered man behind the bar offers a reassuring smile to every patron who enters.”

list.li: Appearance: A short, stocky man in his 30s with sun-darkened skin, cropped brown hair, and a quick, friendly grin. He wears a simple apron over travel-worn clothes.
Personality: Jovial, optimistic, and quick to trust newcomers. Always trying to make strangers feel welcome.

Hook: He came to Phandalin chasing gold in the mines, but soon realized he was better suited to running an inn. He enjoys hearing tales from travelers and quietly worries about how long Phandalin can survive the growing dangers.

text.p: Food:

list.li: Stew of the Day (rabbit or venison, with bread) – 3 sp
Hearth-Baked Loaf & Cheese – 2 sp
Salted Pork with Root Vegetables – 5 sp
Traveler’s Ration Plate (cold meats, bread, dried fruit) – 2 sp
House Ale (tankard) – 4 cp
Dwarven Brew (imported, strong) – 1 sp
Honeyed Mead – 6 cp
House Wine (red, simple) – 8 cp
Watered Cider – 2 cp
Common Room Cot (shared space) – 2 sp/night
Private Room (basic bed, wash basin) – 5 sp/night
Comfort Room (larger bed, small hearth, pitcher of warm water) – 8 sp/night

linklist.link: Book - D&D Dragon of Icespire Peak

text.frame: Barthen’s Provisions sits along the north side of Phandalin’s muddy main street, its stout wooden frame built to last against frontier weather. The building is broad rather than tall, with a low-pitched roof of gray shingles and heavy shutters braced with iron. A wooden sign, carved with the image of a sack and cartwheel, swings gently in the breeze above the front door. Wagons and handcarts are often lined up outside, ruts worn deep into the dirt from years of deliveries. The faint smell of hay and oxen lingers near the hitching posts, and stacked crates wait by the porch, ready to be hauled inside.

*The interior is wide and open, its wooden floorboards smooth from countless boots. Rows of sturdy shelves line the walls and run down the center of the space, stacked with the necessities of frontier life: coiled ropes, lanterns, sacks of flour, crates of dried rations, folded bedrolls, oil flasks, and stacks of roughspun clothing. Barrels of grain and pickled goods rest near the rear, while a set of counters dominates the front of the shop, cluttered with ledgers, scales, and parchment price tags. The air carries the earthy scents of dried herbs, wax, and oiled wood. Lanterns hang from crossbeams overhead, filling the shop with steady, practical light. It feels less like a merchant’s storefront and more like a supply depot — the kind of place where a town’s lifeline is measured in rope lengths, ration sacks, and lantern oil.*

list.li: No Potions available until Adabra returns or agrees to provide potions for the village
Barthen’s isn’t just a supply depot—it’s a vital trading hub in the region, connecting ranchers, miners, and merchants from Phandalin to buyers as distant as Waterdeep
Open from sunup until dusk, Barthen’s is bustling with activity during the day, full of locals stocking up on supplies or adventurers planning their next move

linklist.link: Book - D&D Dragon of Icespire Peak

text.frame: “The inn is thick with anxious voices, but one name rises again and again—Adabra Gwynn. She’s the herbalist who lives alone at Umbrage Hill, a few hours south of town. She’s the only one in miles who can brew healing draughts, and with the caravan’s potions lost, Phandalin’s survival depends on her. But Umbrage Hill is dangerous. A beast’s shadow has been seen circling the skies above it, and folk whisper that no one should travel there alone. The townsfolk plead for someone to reach her, to bring her back or at least make sure she’s safe. All eyes turn to you. If Adabra falls, Phandalin falls with her.”

“An hour into your hike, the air shudders with a deafening roar. It rumbles across the plains from the southeast—the very direction of Umbrage Hill. Birds scatter from the grasses, and for a heartbeat, the land falls silent as though even the earth is holding its breath.”

list.li: Perception DC 12 → Estimate distance (several miles off, not directly on them).
History or Nature DC 15 → Recognize the roar type, but players must guess what beast it belongs to.
Natural 20 on above → They recall tales of a manticore’s bellow.

text.frame: “The windmill of Umbrage Hill rises above the grassy plain, its blades creaking slowly in the breeze. The path bends toward it when a sudden scream rips through the air, followed by the echoing roar of something massive. From the hilltop, a terrified commoner bolts out of the mill’s doorway, sprinting downhill, his face twisted in terror. Above him, a hulking silhouette takes shape against the sky—a monstrous beast with the body of a lion, enormous bat-like wings, and a barbed tail lashing in the air. With a roar, it surges forward, claws outstretched, flying straight for the fleeing commoner. At the same time, another roar thunders from the hilltop. A second creature, its tail slamming against the stone, claws and wings battering the shutters, is savaging the windmill itself—trying to tear its way inside.”

list.li: If successful, the flying manticore is distracted long enough for the commoner to dive out of its reach and survive.
If failed, the manticore rends the fleeing man before the party’s eyes. His screams are silenced in an instant.

text.p: This gives the players agency: save a life or watch the horror unfold.

list.li: Manticore A → airborne, targets the fleeing commoner first, then engages party.
Manticore B → attacking the windmill, focused on reaching Adabra.
Manticores coordinate, one in the air, one on the ground.
If one manticore dies, the other immediately roars in anguish and flees — unwilling to fight without its mate.
If heavily wounded but not killed, either might disengage and retreat into the skies.
If saved → staggers back to safety, clings to the adventurers, thanking them profusely before retreating down the hill.
If killed → his shredded remains reinforce the brutal danger of the frontier.
Bangs on shutters, crying for help.
Screams whenever the second manticore crashes against the windmill.
Survives only if the PCs intervene.

text.frame: The windmill door creaks open, and a woman in her fifties steps out, her face pale and hands still trembling from the assault. She wears a simple alchemist’s apron, dusted with herbs and powders. Her eyes dart to the sky, then settle on you with relief.
“By the gods… I thought I was finished. You have my thanks — if not for you, those beasts would have torn me apart.”

list.li: Adabra quickly regains her composure and folds her arms, setting her jaw.

text.frame: “This windmill is my home. I’ve worked here for years, and I’ll not abandon it because of one attack. I can brew my draughts here just as well as in Phandalin.”

list.li: Persuasion/Reasoning DC 12 → If succeeded, she softens:

text.frame: “…Perhaps you’re right. The roads are too dangerous, and the town needs me alive more than I need these stones. If Phandalin will have me, I’ll go.”
text.p: If failed, she insists on staying:

list.li: “I’ll not be frightened out of my own home. Tell the town I’ll send what potions I can — but I will not leave.”

text.p: While tidying her things, Adabra muses aloud:
text.frame: “Strange, now that I think of it… a wood elf woman passed by not long ago. She left me a recipe for a potion I’d never thought to try. I’ve kept it somewhere here… perhaps back in Phandalin I’d have better luck finding it among my notes.”
text.p: Trigger this if only Kaelen is present

linklist.link: Book - D&D Dragon of Icespire Peak

text.p: As the party relaxes in Stonehill Inn, they overhear two miners gossiping:
text.frame: “You heard about that avalanche a while back? Tore through the foothills southwest — opened up some kind of old dwarven temple. Prospectors are all over it now, sayin’ there’s riches buried deep.”
“Riches, eh? Or curses. Old dwarf gods don’t give up their gold easy.”
text.p: This makes the site feel like local news that’s been circulating for weeks.
Two miners sit hunched over mugs, voices low but eager.
text.frame: “Heard it myself — avalanche tore the side off a hill a few months back. Opened up an old dwarven temple, walls still covered in carvings.”
“Aye, and the prospectors that went in say there’s gold in the stone, relics too. Enough to make a man rich if the gods don’t smite him for takin’ it.”
“Riches don’t lie in the open long. Someone’ll claim it, one way or another.”
text.p: A pair of older townsfolk murmur near the hearth, one crossing himself nervously.
text.frame: “Mark my words, that place should’ve stayed buried. Dwarves build their halls for gods, not for men.”
“The avalanche was no accident. The mountain revealed it because something inside wanted out.”
“Those poor fools digging around there? They’ll wake it, sure as sunrise.”
text.p: When the party asks Tharros Blacktide for advice (or if they seem undecided):
text.frame: “There’s talk of dwarves digging at an old ruin to the southwest. Word is the mountain itself uncovered it, like the gods wanted it seen again. They’re prospectors, not fighters — and prospectors with gold on their minds often draw trouble. If you’re set on making your mark, I’d look their way.”
text.p: This frames Blacktide as a mentor, not a quest-giver — he shares what he’s heard, but doesn’t order the party.

The dwarven excavation lies due east of Leilon, 15 miles southwest of Phandalin, at the eastern end of a canyon (area E1). When the characters reach area E1 on the map, read the following boxed text aloud:
text.frame: The canyon's rocky walls rise to a height of eighty feet. At the end of the canyon, a twenty-foot-high wall of black stone has a broken gate carved into it, with one stone door hanging precariously by a hinge and the other door missing. Beyond this open gate, in the shadow of a great mountain to the east, lies a ruined settlement. All is quiet.
text.p: If the characters announce their arrival, Dazlyn and Norbus come forth to greet them. Otherwise, the characters encounter the dwarves in area E3

list.li: Personality: Cautious but optimistic. Sees opportunity in ruins. Always taking notes on his findings.
Voice Cue: Formal tone, like he’s dictating for a journal.
Opening Line: “Ah, travelers! By Moradin’s beard, you gave us a start. These halls have been long buried — and longer forgotten.”
Personality: Grumpy, suspicious, complains constantly. Less interested in history, more in the potential profit.
Voice Cue: Gravelly and sharp, with a mutter for every situation.
Opening Line: “Bah! More wanderers. Keep your hands off the stone — you’ll bring the whole bloody canyon down on us.”

text.p: Together they form a bickering pair:

list.li: Dazlyn: “There’s history here worth preserving.”
Norbus: “There’s coin here worth taking, you mean.”
If the party calls out, waves, or otherwise announces their arrival → Dazlyn and Norbus appear promptly, dusty from work, relieved to see armed travelers.
Dazlyn greets with formality, Norbus with suspicion.
If the party approaches quietly → They encounter the dwarves at Area E3, where the two are actively clearing rubble.
The dwarves are startled at first, then wary until reassured.
Perception DC 12 → Notice the dwarves’ tracks and scattered tools outside the ruin, signs it’s actively being explored.
Investigation DC 13 → Realize the gates weren’t broken recently — this ruin has been exposed for centuries, the avalanche only revealed it.

text.frame: *“A partially collapsed, ten-foot-high wall separates this courtyard from the canyon settlement behind you. Three heaps of stone and rubble lie scattered across the yard, each casting jagged shadows in the afternoon light. Hewn directly into the canyon’s back wall looms a thirty-foot-high temple facade. A flight of worn steps leads up to a wide stone platform. There, a ten-foot-high doorway gapes open, flanked by life-sized granite statues of cloaked dwarves. Though weatherworn and cracked, their faces remain cruel — lips pulled into sinister grins that seem to mock all who approach.”*
text.h: Overheard Bickering (if party listens before approaching)
text.p: A DC 12 Perception check lets the characters hear voices. If they stop to listen, read:
text.frame: “From behind the eastern rubble pile, two dwarves’ voices echo, bickering in Common with thick accents.” Dazlyn (exasperated): “I’m telling you, the rubble at the back hides more than stone. There could be treasure beneath it — relics, maybe even vaults.” Norbus (snapping): “Or it hides death, you fool! That rubble stays where it lies, or we’ll be buried with it. Don’t think I don’t hear the stone groaning when I sleep.” Dazlyn: “Superstitious nonsense! The temple was built to last. Mark my words — riches are just waiting.” Norbus: “Riches won’t matter if we’re dead! You want to end up like the others that vanished in cursed halls? Not me, lad. Not me.”
text.p: If the party rolls DC 15 Insight or History, they recognize that the dwarves believe there is treasure hidden deeper inside — though Norbus fears traps or collapse.
If the players approach openly

list.li: the dwarves rise, brushing crumbs from their beards, and greet them cautiously.

text.p: If the players sneak or linger

list.li: the dwarves may notice (Passive Perception 10) and react defensively before realizing they’re not alone.

text.p: Dazlyn’s Greeting (forthright):
text.frame: “Ah! Travelers. Don’t suppose you’d lend a hand? These ruins are older than the mountains themselves, and if we’re to see them safely uncovered, we could use some steel at our side.”
text.p: Norbus’ Greeting (gruff):
text.frame: “Steel, pah! What we need is a miracle. Ochre jellies slithering about inside, shadows where shadows don’t belong. You’ve got death written all over your boots if you wander in there.”

linklist.link: Parcel: 06.03.03 E3. Courtyard and Temple Facade

text.p: Arrival
text.frame: *“The ruined doorway opens into a dark, wide chamber. Faint drafts stir the dust, hinting at unseen passages in the walls. Four tall stone pillars rise to support the ceiling, their bases chipped and worn. At the far end stands a limestone altar, its surface cracked and stained a deep, rusted red. Faint scratches mark its face, and something glints faintly in the shadows above. The air is still, heavy with the silence of a place long abandoned.”*

list.li: Each can be detected by the light breeze they emit.
DC 10 Perception (passive allowed) → Notice a draft along the seams.
Each door opens into a narrow passage, except one which hides the pillar cavity.
On the altar lies a staff fragment — a plain, worn piece of dark wood.
A closer look reveals an inscription: “Vaelor” burned faintly into the side in Elvish script.
If Selene is present → this connects directly to her family’s lost staff arc.

text.p: Trigger: As soon as the altar is approached.

list.li: Jellies drop down or slide forward to attack once disturbed.
Their slow movement can be used to build tension (dripping acid, stretching like tar).
Use the altar as part of the environment — adventurers might climb it, knock things down, etc.

text.frame: “With a grinding scrape, the stone panel swings inward. The air stirs cold, and a cascade of ancient skulls clatters out, bouncing across the floor. Beneath them lies a small stone coffer, its lid unlatched, packed with glittering gemstones that catch the dim light.”
text.p: Treasure. The secret door in the pillar conceals a cavity packed with dwarf skulls that tumble out when the door is opened. At the bottom of the cavity is an unlocked stone coffer containing 15 gemstones worth 10 gp each.
Arrival After Clearing Rubble
text.frame: *“The last stones clatter free, and the rubble gives way to a dust-choked chamber beyond. The walls here sag inward, cracked and unstable, with fallen masonry piled in the corners. Two alcoves stand opposite one another: to the south, only the shattered remains of a statue lie scattered across the floor: crushed in the earlier collapse. Also Half-buried in rubble lies the skeleton of a dwarf priest with a small silver chain that glimmers in the faint light, ; to the north, a stone figure of a horned dwarf remains intact, its greedy eyes fixed on a glowing green gem clutched tightly in its hands. The faint light of the gem casts sickly reflections across the broken stone.”*

list.li: The gem is the trigger.
If taken → the gem instantly turns to dust → the statue explodes.
DC 15 Dexterity Save → 22 (4d10) piercing damage on failure, half on success.
Shards of stone blast outward, ripping through the alcove.
Investigation DC 14 → Notice fine cracks around the statue’s chest and arms, suggesting it’s unstable.
Arcana DC 15 → Recognize that the gem’s glow is not innate, but magical — a lure.
Religion DC 12 → Identify the horned dwarf imagery as Abbathor, dwarven god of greed.
Half-buried in rubble lies the skeleton of a dwarf priest, crushed in the earlier collapse.
Rotted red leather armor still clings to the bones, stiff and useless.
Around its neck is a silver chain bearing a holy symbol of Abbathor — a tiny jeweled dagger.
The holy symbol is worth 50 gp.
Inscribed with runes: “Greed is good.”

text.h: Final Scene: Departure from the Excavation
text.p: Dazlyn & Norbus — Payment Discussion
text.frame: “As you gather your things and prepare to leave, the two dwarves shuffle over. Dazlyn clears his throat, brushing stone dust from his beard, while Norbus crosses his arms with a grunt.”

“You’ve done us a fine service. Ochre jellies slain, halls cleared, even secrets uncovered. Now… we’re no thieves, mind you. But fair’s fair. A portion of what you’ve pulled from these stones should go to the excavation. You can keep the lion’s share, of course.”
“Bah, take your gold if you want it. But if you’re running back to Phandalin with your tails tucked, don’t expect us to follow. This ruin’s ours, curse or no.”

list.li: If the party insists they leave: Dazlyn hesitates but agrees with persuasion DC 13; Norbus refuses outright unless bribed or coerced.
If left behind: They remain, stubbornly digging.

text.frame: “You take your leave of the excavation site, the canyon walls narrowing as you retrace the path toward the foothills. Dust crunches underfoot, and the silence of the ruins lingers in your ears. But as you walk, you catch the sound of guttural voices carried on the wind — harsh syllables echoing off stone, growing louder with each passing step.”*
text.p: DC 12 Perception → Party hears the orcs approaching first.
They can prepare, hide, or choose the ground.
Fail → The orcs hear them first and launch an ambush with a surprise round.
text.frame: “A sudden roar of guttural voices erupts as five orcs rush from the rocks, their boots pounding the canyon floor. Weapons raised, their eyes gleam with feral hunger as they crash down upon you!”

linklist.link: Book - D&D Dragon of Icespire Peak

tr.td: “The reclusive rock gnomes in caves to the southeast—Gnomengarde—make magical inventions. They might have something to fight the dragon. Bring back anything useful; if you don’t keep it, I’ll pay 50 gp.”
Persuasion DC 12 → He wants a written note from the gnome rulers or the item itself as proof; he’ll pay on the spot if it’s clearly dragon-fighting gear.
“Travelers swear the gnomes’ gadgets are clever as wizards. If anyone has a trick for that dragon, it’s them—southeast caves.”
Persuasion DC 12 → Directions: take the southeast trail, follow the stream into the foothills; look for hanging spoon-chimes marking their approach.
“The gnomes keep to themselves, but share when need is great. Ask kindly; do not demand. If they aid you against the dragon, honor it.”
Religion DC 12 → Etiquette: announce yourselves, weapons sheathed, offer fair trade or a small gift (wire, oil, fine chalk). Start the talk by naming the dragon threat plainly.
“I’ve supplied them for years—good folk, private. Their caves are southeast in the first rise of the mountains.”
Survival DC 12 → Route notes: cairn at the birch → bear right along the creek cut; when the wall turns slate-dark, the entry is a low arch screened with wind-chimes.
“Gnome trouble slows trade. I like problems solved cleanly.”
Insight DC 13 → Reads her angle: wants confirmation the threat’s ended; a signed note from the rulers earns goodwill (and coin).
“If you return with anything useful vs. a dragon, Harbin’s paying 50 gp. And mind the gnomes’ contraptions—they trap their own halls.”
Investigation DC 12 → Practical tips: carry a tarp and net; tap containers from the side; avoid sparks around metal rigs; don’t yank levers you didn’t set.

text.frame: The passage opens into a low grotto where a waterfall booms into a black, knee-deep pool. Mist drifts across two squat islands carpeted with oversized mushrooms—red caps slick with oil, green fronds dusted like flour, and dusky purple bulbs beaded with moisture. Rope-and-pulley lanterns sway overhead; their halos wobble in the spray. A narrow rope bridge spans to a stone landing on the far side.

list.li: Ceiling ~7 ft; Mediums feel cramped with tall gear; Larges are squeezing.
Noise: hearing-based Perception disadvantage in sight of the falls; must raise voices.
Water: 3 ft deep = difficult terrain; slick ledges → first sudden turn/Dash: Dex (Acrobatics) DC 10 or fall prone.
Mushrooms (quick use): Red→lamp oil (10 min = 1 flask), Green→rations (1 day, needs drying), Purple→wine must (ferments later).

text.frame: As you near the bridge—or call out—three gnomes step onto the far anchor. Toolbelts and patchwork leathers; crossbows slung, not aimed. One raises a tin speaking-horn. “Hallo there! Gnomengarde approach. Please pause—names and business, if you please. The bridge is tricky footing.” Another rests a hand near a brass bell—habit more than threat. The third watches your footing rather than your blades.

list.li: Bridge stats: 35-ft span; anchors 20 ft high; midpoint 15 ft above water; difficult terrain; water below midpoint 5 ft deep (fall/jump there: no damage). Bridge AC 11, 30 HP, immune poison/psychic.
Barrel crabs (G6): cannot cross.

Persuasion DC 12 (names/purpose; −2 DC if they cite Harbin’s safety check or “here to help”). Success: parley continues; a spokesperson may step 5–10 ft onto the span. Fail: bell jingle (not alarm), request proof or single speaker → fresh Persuasion DC 10.
Produce proof: Sleight of Hand DC 10 to place letter on near post (or Mage Hand, no roll). Success: controlled crossing—one at a time, peace-bonded weapons.
Read the sentries: Insight DC 10 to clock procedural vs curious; next social check advantage.
Safety gesture: Prestidigitation/Gust to dry first planks → next Persuasion advantage.
De-escalation: Only full ring if rushed/menaced or a second failure; otherwise procedure > violence.
On success: They fetch a guide to escort you inside → Scene 3.

text.frame: Your guide halts at a doorway. Inside, two rock gnomes argue in rapid-fire Gnomish amid cluttered tables and half-finished contraptions. One waves a copper tube; the other brandishes a bundle of buckles and canvas. A ten-foot ledge at the back holds a pedestal with a leather-bound book. They notice you. The apron gnome sighs, “Visitors! Please tell me you’re not here to build a ‘sanity ray.’”

list.li: Foremost inventors: Fibblestib (wants a sanity ray) and Dabbledob (prefers a straitjacket).
They prioritize curing Korboz / rescuing Gnerkli over the missing-gnomes mystery.
Promise magical rewards for effective help.
Korboz was attacked by a 10-ft rug in G14; creature mimics Medium objects (chairs, chests, doors/wall bulges).
Orryn & Warryn vanished; no remains.
Gnomes poke objects with nonmagical wands, then flee at danger.
Persuasion DC 12 to redirect them from devices to immediate hunt → they escort and provide poking poles.
Insight or Medicine DC 11 to frame calm/safety plan → advantage on next social check with them.
Arcana/Investigation DC 12 to “de-fang” the sanity ray (diagnostic light) → advantage once on an Investigation to spot mimic residue.

text.p: Offer: Gnomes will poke objects with nonmagical wands but flee at first sign of danger.
text.h: Gnome Kings’ Bedroom (Front Door Block / Panic)
text.frame: A stout iron-banded door bars the way. From within, a strained voice calls through the bolts: “I am King Korboz. Do not enter. The— the rug in the throne room attacked us. We are… secure. Leave at once.” You hear another gnome murmur, then the clink of a flask.

list.li: Front door: Locked. Only Korboz and Gnerkli have keys.
Secret entry: Hidden from Throne Room (G14); intentional search Perception DC 10 (per your secret-door rule).
Inside: Korboz (jagged crown, patchwork cloak) clutching a solvent flask; Gnerkli glued to a chair (restrained); comfortable gnome bedroom.
He will only say: “A rug attacked me in the throne room. Leave.”
He will not say “shapechanger” unless pressed.

text.p: Persuasion DC 12 or Insight DC 10 (showing calm, safety-first plan) → Korboz elaborates: the “rug” changed, and he fears it can look like other things (shapechanger implication).

list.li: Failure: he stonewalls and repeats “Leave.” Further pressure risks alarm.

text.p: If the party claims the threat is dealt with: Persuasion DC 12 to reassure.

list.li: Success: He speaks plainly, may unglue Gnerkli (solvent; object interaction) and allow mediated entry later.
Fail: Remains locked down; pushing harder raises alarm.

p.b: If the party uses the secret door to enter now

text.p: Korboz orders them out immediately.
De-escalate: Persuasion DC 12 (advantage if hands visible, weapons peace-bonded).

list.li: Success: He tolerates a brief explanation; agrees to wait while they investigate.
Fail: He rings for help; stance turns hostile and social DCs across Gnomengarde increase by +4 until repaired.

text.p: Confirms: rug attack in G14, Orryn & Warryn missing, and a fearful belief the attacker can take other forms (only after prying).
text.h: Investigation Loop (Choose 2–3 Clues, Then Converge on G8)
text.frame: “Scrapes mar the floor—drag lines that stop at a rocky bulge that doesn’t match the wall.”
“Barrels stand in neat rows. One sits a half-inch proud of a chalk outline and lacks a tap hole.”
“Boot scuffs trail to a wardrobe set two inches off square; no blood, no struggle.”
“A bare square on the stone shows a faint slick—where a large rug once lay.”
text.p: Safe prodding: Any suspicious object can be poked; no roll to provoke. If it’s the mimic, it reacts.
Scans: Perception or Investigation DC 12 to spot tells (viscous sheen, mismatched hinge pins, drag that ends at object).
False positives: In wild-magic rooms, Arcana DC 10–12 can spook them with harmless quirks.
Gnome escorts: They grant Help on one object-scan, then skitter back.
text.frame: Among the stacked crates and neat rows of barrels, one barrel’s shadow clings a little too long to the floor. Its hoops look… soft, somehow—like knuckles trying to be wood.
The staves ripple. A wet seam peels open into a maw. A burbling voice gurgles, “Hh… hungry. Trade?”
text.p: Triggering it: Poke/touch/linger adjacent → it lashes out; otherwise you can attempt parley if using the variant.
Parley (variant): Cha (Intimidation or Persuasion) DC 15 to compel it to leave Gnomengarde.

p.b: Advantage with a credible threat (fire/acid on ready) or a food bribe (fresh meat/game).

list.li: Success: It oozes out under escort; counts as solving the threat (kings still reward).
Fail: It feints, then ambushes the weakest target.

text.p: Read-Aloud (success)
text.frame: Word spreads fast; the halls buzz with relieved chatter. King Korboz unclenches, and the gnomes bring out a lacquered chest of curios. “You’ve done us a great service. Take a boon from Gnomengarde—and our thanks.”
text.p: Success conditions: Slain or compelled to leave under escort.
Rewards (pick 1–2 items): Hat of Wizardry, Wand of Pyrotechnics, Clockwork Amulet, Pole of Collapsing, or your preferred canon stash.
Reputation: Advantage on future social checks with Gnomengarde; access to simple clockwork trinkets.
If failure/retreat: After 1 hour, the mimic relocates and claims another gnome that night; increase urgency and patrols; investigation resets with 1 fresh clue.

tr.td: “High Road’s jumpy—bandits took a team last tenday.”
Persuasion DC 12 → rough ambush spot marked; Survival DC 12 to plan a detour.
“Your wagon’s ready in Leilon; ox called Brindle’s temperamental.”
Animal Handling DC 11 → tips for calming Brindle; grants advantage once.
“Guild wants the job, not the Exchange. Expect… competition.”
Insight DC 12 → it’s a rival crew, not assassins; you can propose traveling together.
“Storms brewing. Tymora favors prudence over speed.”
Religion DC 10 → blessing; 1 PC gains +1d4 to a single travel check.
Intimidation DC 12 or Persuasion DC 13 → he admits two caravans are late.
“Old bandit sign near the Triboar turn. Fresh.”
Survival DC 12 → spot the sign; grants advantage vs the first ambush Stealth.
“Mountain’s Toe is dry till tools arrive. Foreman’s on edge.”
Insight DC 12 → foreman blames skimming; seeds ledger subplot.
“Miss Thornton says keep the sealed crate sealed.”
Investigation DC 12 → crate weight matches ledgers, not metal; curiosity hook.
“Fake toll north of the barrow stones—watch for painted badges.”
Perception DC 12 → what the forgeries look like; advantage to call their bluff.
Nature DC 12 → likely griffon or hippogriff; chance event table entry unlocked.
10 gp prototype → one‑use auto‑brake; grants advantage vs runaway cart mishap.
“Bet you can’t race the High Road in a day!”
Persuasion DC 10 → he instead draws a useful shortcut (save 1–2 hours on dry ground).

text.frame: “You look capable. Fetch a prepaid shipment of pickaxes, shovels, spikes, rope, oil, lanterns from Leilon. Deliver to me at the Miner’s Exchange. Base 100 gp on receipt. +50 gp if it’s here within two days and nothing goes missing. If you’ll press on to Mountain’s Toe same day, add +75 gp. Simple. Professional. Interested?”

p.b: Private Office Offer (door closed, lower voice):

text.frame: “There is also a sealed crate. You will not open it. No detours, no prying hands. Handle it discreetly and I’ll include a 25 gp quiet fee. Bring me the Exchange receipt and the crate, unopened, and we’ll be friends.”

list.li: • Insight DC 12: She’s testing reliability, not muscle.
• Insight DC 14: The crate matters more than the tools.
• If PCs ask what’s inside: “Accounts.” She does not elaborate.

p.b: Hardball Mode (if the party haggles or postures):

list.li: Persuasion DC 13: Raise the rush bonus to +75 gp or convert +50 gp into goods at cost (Lionshield/Barthen’s).
Deception DC 13 (claim rival interest/experience): Add +10 gp hazard stipend and one healer’s kit.
Intimidation DC 14: Immediate +25 gp but –1 standing with Halia (future jobs start cool).

text.p: Offer a concession: Promise written inventory on arrival → she waives crate loss penalties up to 10 gp.
Push your luck (second demand): Further raises require a cost (longer inspection on delivery, or she assigns a rival crew to “share” the road).

p.b: If the sealed crate is opened:

list.li: Opened but intact delivery: Pays half; marks the crew unreliable. Future jobs dock –25 gp until redeemed.
Missing or damaged: Pays half at most and quietly warns friends; a Zhent-leaning fixer offers the party a shady buyout next session.
Handled perfectly: Adds a one‑time favor chit: advantage on one future negotiation with her.

linklist.link: Parcel: Episode#0.04.00 Leilon's Supply Run Parcel

text.p: Choose or roll 1 travel hazard, 1 social complication, 1 hostile encounter.

list.li: 1. Broken Axle: Cart save vs ruts (Dex check by driver DC 12). On fail, a wheel cracks; repair with Tinker’s Tools or Carpenter’s Tools DC 12 and a repair kit (1 hour).
2. Flooded Ford: Choose to detour (+6 hours) or cross (Athletics DC 12 to guide oxen; on fail, 1d4 crates soak—oil ruined unless salvaged with Sleight of Hand DC 12).
3. Sudden Storm: Disadvantage on Perception checks for 1 watch; soaked road halves travel for 6 hours.
4. Fallen Tree: Clear (Athletics DC 13, 30 minutes) or bypass (Animal Handling DC 12).
5. Crate Shift: Hard brake; Dex saves DC 12 for riders on wagon or take 1d4.
6. Road Blockade (fake): See Social Complications #1.
1. Road Tollers: “Guard” patrol demands a toll (Insight DC 12 spots forged badges). Parley (Persuasion/Intimidation DC 13) or fight 1–2 bandits + 1 thug.
2. Refugee Ask: Family requests a lift. Accept (goodwill in Phandalin; wagon speed −2 miles) or decline (no penalty).
3. Caravan Guild Claim: A rival team claims Halia promised them the job. Produce paperwork (Investigation DC 12) or outbid (10 gp) or agree to travel together (shared encounter).
4. Zhent Strings: If asked, Halia hints to keep the sealed crate sealed; a shady contact at Barthen’s tries to buy it for 25 gp.
5. Sick Ox: Stablehand in Leilon sold a feverish animal; Animal Handling DC 12 to nurse it; on fail, pace −4 miles/day unless swapped at a hamlet (10 gp).
6. Lost Ledger: The foreman at Mountain’s Toe mislaid last month’s chit; minor delay while it’s found (Investigation DC 12 or Persuasion DC 12 to accept provisional receipt).
1. Goblin Ambush: 4–6 goblins target the driver (use cover).
2. Bandit Crossfire: 4 bandits + 1 scout; objective is cargo, not murder.
3. Wolves at Dusk: 5 wolves harry oxen; they flee if 2 drop.
4. Twig Blight Tangle: 8 twig blights in a muddy stretch; carts risk bogging (Str checks DC 12).
5. Orc Skirmishers: 3 orcs testing the road; loud, direct.
6. Manticore Pass-by: Nonlethal flyover—Intimidation/Animal Handling DC 13 to keep oxen calm or lose 1 hour corralling.

text.p: This trigger for the Broken Axle and Goblin Ambush encounters
Base pay: 100 gp on signed receipt at Miner’s Exchange.
Bonus: +50 gp if delivered in ≤2 days with no crate losses and the sealed crate intact; +75 gp extra if the party pushes on and delivers to Mountain’s Toe the same day.
Partial: If 1–2 crates lost/destroyed, reduce pay by 10 gp per crate (Halia’s discretion).
Failure: If the sealed crate is opened or missing, Halia pays half and becomes frosty; Zhent complications later.

list.li: Spotless delivery: +1 standing with Miner’s Exchange; gossip in Stonehill Inn admires the party.
Losses/late: Halia spreads a cool but cutting review; other jobs dock pay until the party redeems themselves.

text.p: Quest Brief (in town)
Hook: Reports of attacks near Conyberry; survivors mention highwaymen.
Objective: Clear the area of bandit threats.
Reward: 300 gp upon return.
Leads: “They set on travelers along the Triboar Trail, then melt back toward Conyberry.”
text.h: Scene 1 — Road to Conyberry (Highwaymen vs. Seraphine)
text.frame: The trail narrows between scrub oaks and a tall shrubs. Ahead, rough voices cut the quiet—jeers, orders, the scrape of steel. A wrecked wagon lies half-spilled in the ditch, its broken axle gray with dust. Dark wine stains spider the dirt in dried fans—old, sticky patches that crack underfoot. Ten paces beyond the wreck, a cloaked woman stands with a plain travel staff held crosswise as three men circle in. Her robe is well-mended but dignified—earthy greens stitched with vine and wheat motifs—and a wooden holy symbol of Chauntea rests at her collar. Her tone is calm, steady: “No one needs to bleed today. Take a breath.” One bandit flicks a dagger toward a leather satchel at her feet. Another draws his blade and flurries it, another has his bow half-drawn, eyes cutting toward you as you crest the rise. A fourth lingers back with a whistle between two fingers, waiting to signal. Dust hangs in the evening light. The road is narrow. If steel flashes, there’s barely room to swing.
text.h: Scene 1.5 — Surrender on the Road (Mercy Fork)
text.frame: Steel clatters to the dirt. One bandit drops to his knees, hands raised, eyes wide and wet. “Mercy! I yield! I’m done—please.” Seraphine steps between blades and the kneeling man, palm out. “Hold. No more blood. Let him speak.” Dust hangs in the quiet; a jay calls from the scrub. The bandit swallows, trembling, waiting on your word.

p.b: A) Mercy & Release (sets up ambush later)

text.p: Persuasion DC 13 (Seraphine or a PC; Seraphine present grants advantage).

list.li: Success: You accept the surrender and let him go with a warning or terms. He runs to Conyberry to gather reinforcements and prepare an ambush (use your Scene 2A).
Fail: He panics, tries to bolt anyway → see Chase below, or party may switch to B/C.

p.b: B) Mercy with Conditions (reduces ambush severity)

text.p: Set terms (pick 1–2): drop the whistle, map the lookout posts, carry a message to the captain, leave the region.
Intimidation or Persuasion DC 14 to make terms stick.

list.li: Success: Ambush still happens, but -2 bandits or no snares/grease (choose one).
Fail: He agrees, then reneges (treat as A).

p.b: C) Take Prisoner (no ambush, harder social later)

text.p: Bind and escort or send him back to town.
Intimidation DC 12 to keep him compliant on the march.
Effect: No ambush at Conyberry; the captain confronts openly (Scene 2B), but local rumors paint the party as hardliners (future Charisma checks in the region +2 DC unless you roleplay mercy later).
Insight (DC 12): Is the surrender genuine?
Success: He’s truly scared; won’t rejoin if freed with stern warning (treat as B-success but with -1 bandit only).
Persuasion DC 12 or Intimidation DC 12 → gets a quick intel packet (pick 2):
1. Whistle codes: two short, one long = “all-in”.
2. Captain’s sign: red-slashed sash or ring.
3. Kill zone lane between collapsed cottages.
4. Perch markers (chalk X) on ruined walls.
Stabilize foes: Medicine DC 10 to keep downed bandits alive (Seraphine will help). Doing so earns her favor later.

p.b: Chase / Bolt (if he runs during failure)

text.p: He uses Dash into scrub.
Group contest: Athletics or Acrobatics vs. DC 12 (party) to catch before he vanishes; on two successes before two failures, they grab him.
Failure: he escapes → treat as A (ambush).

p.b: Evidence & Loot on the Surrendered Bandit

text.p: Signal whistle, 2d10 cp, 1d6 sp, and a chalk-sketched lane (kill zone) on bark or scrap. If you accepted terms, he leaves these behind.
A – Release: Full ambush at Conyberry (Scene 2A).
B – Conditional Mercy (success): Ambush weaker (-2 bandits or no traps).
C – Prisoner: No ambush; open confrontation (Scene 2B), but regional social checks +2 DC until you repair reputation.

list.li: “Mercy now spares more lives later.”
“Lay down the whistle and walk—prove there’s some good left.”
“Bind him and be done, if you must—but no more killing today.”
If party is spoiling for a fight: Let surrender happen but add a time pressure (“Hoofbeats—others may be near”).
If party leans mercy: Reward with advantage on the first Investigation/Perception DC 12 to spot ambush signs at Conyberry.

text.p: Read-Aloud (stinger):
text.frame: The river curves around Conyberry’s bones—tumbled cottages, roofless walls, and a broken span where a bridge once crossed. Only blackened pilings and a half-fallen arch remain, jutting like ribs over the ford. Wind moves through tall reeds; crows watch from a splintered lintel. No voices. No footprints. Just the hush of water over stones. The lane from the river cuts between two ruined walls toward a narrow choke—cleared of loose rubble, suspiciously tidy. A length of shattered parapet leans at an angle above the lane like a crooked jaw. You step into the gap and—there’s a snap of rope, a hiss of counterweights—something heavy whips down from above. Each creature in the 10-ft square kill zone makes a Dexterity saving throw, DC 16. • Fail: A weighted falling net slams down—restrained and surprised. • Success: You spring clear to the edge—not restrained and not surprised. From the ruins, a sharp whistle—two short, one long—answers the thud of the net.
text.p: Read-Aloud (stinger):
text.frame: The river braids around Conyberry’s ruins, whispering over stones where a bridge once stood. Only blackened pilings and a collapsed arch jut from the current like ribs. Reeds hiss in the wind; waterlight flickers across roofless walls and shattered lintels. You spot movement: a pair of bandits ghost along the far bank, lantern shuttered to a knife-thin beam that sweeps the ford and the broken road beyond. Another figure paces the near side, bootheels crunching grit along a toppled wall. Every so often a soft whistle—one note only—passes between them, answered by the click of a shutter and the scrape of leather on stone. The lane from the river is half-cleared, suspiciously tidy, but the ground around it is a tangle of cover—knee-high reeds, a fallen cart axle, a spine of collapsed masonry. The lantern’s cone carves slow arcs; between sweeps, the ruins fall back into gray and shadow. You can smell pitch and old smoke. Somewhere, a crow ticks its beak against wood. From here, you could belly through the reeds along the waterline, hug the shadowed side of a broken cottage, or wait for the lantern to pass and slip across the open gap before the next whistle. The patrol turns. The light narrows. The moment is yours.
text.h: Scene 2B — Captain’s Surrender (Mercy or Line in the Sand)
text.frame: Blood slicks the captain’s sleeve. He staggers back from the doorway, spits dust, and throws his cutlass down so it skitters across cracked stone. Two fingers rise to his lips—one sharp whistle—and the remaining men freeze. He lifts both hands, palms out. “Enough. You’ve got it. Conyberry’s yours.” His eyes flick from your blades to the broken lane, then back. “Let me walk. I’ll call them off. No more tolls. No more road work. We’re done.” Silence steals into the ruins—just the river and a crow’s dry click. The bandits shift, watching you. Seraphine steps forward a pace, staff low, gaze fixed on you rather than him. “This is the moment,” she says, steady. “Mercy—or example.”
text.p: The captain orders the rest to drop arms and leave.
Persuasion DC 13 (any party face; Seraphine’s presence grants advantage) to bind the terms: quit Conyberry and no more tolls.

list.li: Success: They disperse. Count the quest complete; gather proof (sash, ledger, surrendered whistles).
Fail: A few stragglers peel off to harry you later (treat as a minor road encounter in a future session).

text.p: Seraphine stays with the party. She’ll help treat the wounded (stabilize checks succeed automatically this scene) and travels on.
If the captain is killed after surrender, remaining bandits break or fight to the death (your call).
Seraphine leaves the group at journey’s next safe point: “I won’t walk this road with you.” (You can reintroduce her later after a significant atonement/mercy deed.)

text.p: Cryovain the young white dragon is a roaming threat that can be encountered almost anywhere. Each time the characters arrive at a location tagged on the map of the Sword Coast or prepare to leave that location, roll a d20 and consult the Dragon's Location table to determine Cryovain's current whereabouts. Make your first roll on the table when the adventurers leave Phandalin for the first time.

When the dragon visits a location that is not its lair, it surveys the location from the sky, beyond the reach of ranged weapon attacks. If it spots nothing it can eat, it flies off after circling the location for a minute or two. If it spots something tasty, such as a mule, a horse, or a character, the dragon swoops down and attacks it. Once the dragon kills something, it grabs the carcass and flies off with it. Whatever it takes is then eaten within the hour.

If Cryovain loses more than 10 hit points in battle, the dragon disengages from combat and retreats to its lair at Icespire Hold, remaining there until it finishes a long rest and regains all its hit points. Only at Icespire Hold does the dragon fight to the death.

text.p: A. Raid
B. Sacrifice
create handouts via player notes share with all
lessen stall words. pauses are acceptable. try to focus on story telling
Ceiling: 18ft fight
Doors: Interior doors are made of wood branded with iron. All can be locked and or barred. DC 20 STR to broken
Floors: All made of white stone
Light: Due to its many windows it is brightly lit and dimly lit at night. With reienforced shutters closed, Light during the day become dim light and during the night it be comes dark
Locks: All locks require theives tools and open DC 15 DEX

Windows: Oversized windows on theground level allow light and air to pass easily into the tower. They stand 3ft from the fround and are 6ft tall and 8ft wide. Shutters reinforced with iron bands permit the windows to be shut and barred.
text.frame: Feathergale Spire rises from a pillar of rock high into the air, the tallest point for miles. Built from white limestone and embellished in marble, the spire resembles a gleaming sword that pierces the sky. The gatehouse faces the opposite cliff, its drawbridge the only apparent point of entry. Tall, wide windows encompass the bottom level of the tower, absent only upon the gatehouse side. A circle of open stalls rings the towers foundation where it meets the rock. Above each stall, the sculpture of a hippogriff in flight leaps from the towers base. Beneath Feathergale Spire to the east, a wide gusty canyon yawns through the hills.

A gap of twenty feet separates the ledge where the path ends from the closed drawbridge on Feathergale Spire. The space between the cliffs edge and the gatehouse drops several hundred feet to the bottom of the canyon. Near the ledge, a brass bell hangs from a wooden post.
text.p: The party (with the Wyndwyrds) arrives at the end of a narrow stone bridge spanning a wind-lashed ravine. As the bell's chime echoes across the cliffs, a strange stillness follows. Then — the faint sound of chains grinding. The gate begins to lower, its gears groaning against the constant wind. A lone figure steps onto the bridge — tall, poised, wind-tossed cloak trailing behind her. She walks with grace and discipline, each step measured, ceremonial.
Savra Belabranta.

Her polished armor catches the sun, her long platinum braid swings with the wind. Her face is composed — until her eyes fall on Eren. A flicker of something real breaks through her perfect mask: surprise, recognition... and a flash of guilt.
SAVRA (calmly, tightly): “...Eren. I did not expect to see you here.”
Eren steps forward, hesitating just a moment.
EREN (quietly, hopeful) “It’s been months. I thought you—”
She raises a hand gently, not cold — just... not here.
SAVRA (reassuring but guarded) “We’ll talk. I promise. Just... not yet.”
She doesn’t a hug. No smile. Her tone is official — but the way she looks at him lingers just a moment too long. She turns to address the rest of the group:

p.i: “The Feathergale Society welcomes the Wyndwyrds — and your... company. You arrive safely. That is all that matters. Please follow me”

text.p: She takes an about face and leads the party across the bridge and into the spire. There’s a subtle tension to her posture now, as if she's reining in emotion beneath the surface. A second figure steps forward from the shade of the spire — an Air genasi in iron clad armor, His arms folded as they approach .
Tywin Terrorwind, First Lieutenant of the Spire.
He leans to Savra, every inch of him is control, presence, and command.
TYWIN : “We were expecting performers. Not armed travelers.”
There’s no hostility in his voice — just iron professionalism, and a hint of disapproval. His eyes linger on the wizard’s staff, the cleric’s sigil, the fighters' weapons.
Before anyone in the party can speak, Savra cuts cleanly in:

p.i: “They are with me. As Commander Thurl would say, the wind brings who it must.”

text.p: (She does not look back at Tywin as she says it.)
There’s a flicker of tension.
Tywin’s jaw tenses. His eyes narrow.

But he says nothing. He steps aside — deliberately, silently — and allows the moment to pass but eyes at the armed travelers momentarily before following them in and waves the gate keepers to close the gates.

p.i: “Come. The Spire stands ready to receive you. Rooms have been prepared. The Society values harmony — and you’ve brought music, after all.”

text.p: Her voice softens slightly on that last line. The wind gusts across the bridge again, sending dust swirling around her boots. As the gate grinds to a close.

list.li: Insight DC 10: Savra is clearly surprised and holding back emotion.
Insight DC 13: She wants to reconnect, but isn’t comfortable doing it publicly.
Insight DC 15 (on Tywin): He’s irritated, but not enough to cause trouble — unless it happens again.

text.p: As the great gate closes behind you, the howling wind fades into a haunting hush. A faint breeze still stirs the air - not wild, but controlled, deliberate. You find yourselves standing in a forty five-foot-long hall of gleaming white stone. The walls are smooth, the floor polished to a mirror sheen. Every line in the architecture feels purposeful - like the whole space was carved to guide the wind itself. At the far end of the hall stand two massive, twelve-foot-tall doors, twin reflections of the gate you just passed through. They are seamless, steel-banded, and inscribed with curling feather motifs - less military, more ceremonial. Above you, suspended by thick chains, hangs a breathtaking sight:

A giant eagle, carved from a single timber, its wings of steel folded tight against its sides. The head is crafted from solid steel, polished to a mirror shine. It gazes down with cold, unblinking eyes - part guardian, part warning. It doesn't move, but it feels like it watches. The air here is unnaturally clean. No dust. No scent. The only sounds are the soft creaks of armor and the echo of your own footsteps.
Savra, walking ahead, turns gracefully and says with quiet pride:

p.i: "The Spire's heart opens to the wind and closes to the unworthy. You are guests - and so, the doors remain open."

text.p: Tywin, behind her, adds in a voice like a drawn blade:

list.li: Perception (DC 13): The chains holding the eagle are not just ornamental - they're rigged with tension, like a trap waiting to fall.
Arcana (DC 12): The breeze is magical - it circulates in a deliberate rhythm, likely bound to the Spire itself.
Insight (DC 12 on Savra): She's proud of this space, but that flicker in her eyes when she looks at Eren... she's holding back something.

text.p: Savra leads the party up the spiral stair, each step echoing faintly in the stone as the wind fades behind them. At the landing, she pushes open a pair of finely carved wooden doors, revealing the Great Hall. It curves along the outer edge of the tower, spanning half its diameter, illuminated by light pouring in from overlarge windows that offer a breathtaking view of the valley beyond. Between each window hang tapestries depicting Feathergale knights soaring through the skies on hippogriffs:

list.li: Locked in midair jousts
Slaying dragons high above the clouds
Saluting as they dive from great heights

text.p: Mounted above the tapestries are the heads of griffons, wyverns, owlbears, and manticores, preserved with near-fanatical precision. Their glassy eyes glint in the firelight from twin hearths that bookend the chamber. A long, curved dining table dominates the room, already set for a feast - silver polished to gleam, crystal goblets lined with faint mist from chilled drinks, and the faint scent of herbs and roasted meats hangs in the air. Savra glances back at the group, her voice carefully composed:

SAVRA: "This is our Great Hall - where the Society gathers, dines, and recounts the stories of those who rise above the earth." She gestures behind the party, toward a hallway opposite the feasting table. "Your quarters are just down that hall - quiet, clean, and spacious enough for you all. You'll find fresh water and linens. The wind doesn't carry dust through our halls."

p.i: "Rest while you can. The sky tests us all - and always without warning."

list.li: Perception (DC 12): The mounted heads seem to be positioned to watch the feast table - unnerving if you notice it.
Insight (DC 13): Savra's pride in the Spire is real… but she avoids looking at the beast heads too long.
Investigation (DC 14): One tapestry (the "dragon slaying" one) hides a small, embroidered air elemental glyph along the cloudline.

text.p: With a final spiral ascent, the white stone stairs open into a round stone gazebo - its columns open to the wind, its vaulted ceiling narrowing into a needle-thin minaret that reaches for the sky. The air is cooler here. Sharper. Cleaner. Beyond the gazebo lies the apex of Feathergale Spire - a perfectly flat, circular lawn of soft green grass that shouldn't grow so high above the world. Yet it does. Four white stone paths split the lawn in a compass-rose pattern, each ending at a sharp, decorative crenellation. Between them, the wind flows freely, unimpeded. Set at the eastern edge of the pinnacle, a spyglass mounted on a brass tripod points downward - aimed toward the canyons and hills below. From this vantage, the world stretches in all directions: the canyons of the Sighing Valley to the East, the winding Dessarin River to the south, and the Sumber Hills rolling out beyond the horizon in dusty golden waves.
Savra, gesturing outward: "From here, the Spire sees all. The sky grants clarity - to those willing to rise."

As she steps aside, a tall figure turns from the spyglass. Commander Thurl Merosska Appears He is tall, broad-shouldered, with a chiseled face that carries the calm of command. His cloak flutters gently in the wind, and his hair - pale gold, streaked with silver - is neatly swept back. His armor gleams in the sun, adorned not with symbols of rank, but with a single silver feather at the shoulder. When he speaks, his voice is rich and measured - like someone accustomed to being heard.

THURL (smiling): "You've brought music… and mystery." (He steps forward with open arms - equal parts welcome and evaluation.) "I am Thurl Merosska, commander of the Feathergale Society. The sky watches kindly on your arrival." He studies each of you - appraising without being overt. "We seldom receive guests so late in the season. But when the wind brings travelers to our doorstep, it is rarely by chance." He offers a short bow - courteous, practiced. "You'll join us for a meal, of course. And perhaps… you'll find what you didn't know you were seeking."

list.li: Insight (DC 13): Thurl is charismatic and confident - but behind the warmth, he is calculating everything.
Perception (DC 12): The grass on the pinnacle is perfect - no weeds, no insects, no dirt. Almost like it's grown under ritual control.
Arcana (DC 14): There's a faint magical residue near the spyglass - divination magic, regularly used.
Thurl is visibly pleased.
They are granted a few hours to rest, clean up, or roam the Spire freely before the meal.
Savra will personally walk them back to their rooms and make a comment to Eren about speaking privately later.

text.p: Thurl politely, but firmly, insists:

p.i: "I must strongly advise against travel at this hour. The winds grow unpredictable after sunset."

text.p: If they persist:

list.li: Weather conditions intensify (narratively or magically).
Tywin offers no aid in preparing their departure.
Savra remains silent - obviously uncomfortable.
Persuasion DC 18 or Insight DC 15 may hint that they are not prisoners, but they are no longer trusted.

text.p: Description: A beautifully polished brass spyglass mounted on a tripod, aimed toward the canyons and the Sumber Hills.

list.li: Arcana DC 13: Detects faint traces of divination magic lingering on the lens.
Investigation DC 14 (while inspecting it): On the brass plate at the base, an inscription:

p.i: “So that the Sky’s will may be known. – Y.C.B.”

text.p: (DC 15 Religion reveals “Y.C.B.” may refer to Yan-C-Bin, the Prince of Evil Air — though it’s extremely obscure.)
Description: The grass atop the tower is perfect, green, without soil stains or insect damage.

list.li: Nature DC 12 / Arcana DC 13: Reveals it’s not natural grass — it’s magically grown and maintained, possibly through elemental influence.

Perception DC 14 (while pacing): If viewed from a higher position (e.g. minaret stairs), the stone paths and grass form a spiral pattern — reminiscent of the air cult symbol, but only visible from above.

p.b: 3. A Weather Log in a Viewing Alcove

text.p: Location: Inside the gazebo section, tucked near a bench or small side table is a logbook with neat, military entries.
Entries include:

list.li: “Skywatch successful. Glyph set. Valley remains compliant.”
“Sighing Valley winds stable after last offering. Elemental pressure waning.”
“Knight-Lieutenant Savra observed ritual. Reports potential in new recruits.”

text.p: Investigation DC 13: Reveals a torn-out page at the back.
Imprint visible with charcoal rubbing:

list.li: “Weather shift near Sacred Stone. Thurl recommends retaliation.”

text.p: Optional Player Clues:

list.li: Insight DC 12 (on Thurl’s speech): He speaks like someone rehearsed — someone trying to inspire belief more than offer truth.
Passive Perception 14+: The spyglass isn't aimed at the most active valley trails, but at a seemingly unimportant stretch of open land — maybe where something isn't supposed to be seen.

text.p: The door to Thurl’s quarters opens with a soft groan — oiled hinges, barely used. The air inside is warm from the glow of a fire, crackling low in a marble hearth. The room is refined, but not cluttered: a large bed with feather-down pillows, a closet with riding cloaks and crisp white uniforms, a dark mahogany writing desk, and a tightly shut wooden chest. A small tapestry hangs on the far wall — a stylized depiction of the four winds spiraling around a single silver feather. It is quiet. Perfect. Almost too perfect.
On its surface, clean parchment, a silver quill, and a cylindrical leather case with a stamped seal — the spiral feather emblem.
Inside the case:
text.frame: Merosska, We are pleased to hear about the outcome of your altercation with the Black Earth cult, and we praise you for the capture of one of their prisoners. This noblewoman from Waterdeep has an interesting tale to tell, and we shall enjoy interrogating her further. Keep a close watch on the Sacred Stone Monastery. I want to know what our enemy is planning next. —Your beloved queen, Aerisi Kalinoth

list.li: History DC 13: “Aerisi Kalinoth” is not a noble known in Waterdeep or the surrounding region — strange, given her commanding tone.
Insight DC 12: The phrase “beloved queen” is not romantic — it’s religious or ritualistic. A title of worship.
Locked (Simple, DC 12 to open)
Ornate ceremonial dagger with elemental air sigils
A silken sash with the phrase “Sky above, stone below” embroidered in Auran
A parchment map showing the Sacred Stone Monastery with a feather-shaped stamp over it
Investigation DC 16: A hidden compartment in the chest contains a partchment map of the Sighing Valley with an X marked on a ravine East of the spire
On closer inspection, the spiral of wind contains four elemental symbols — but only the air symbol is complete.
Arcana or Religion DC 14: The arrangement resembles an unfinished elemental node, a cult ritual design.

text.p: This chamber is austere — utilitarian in every way. White stone walls. Unadorned floors. The only warmth comes from a barely burning coal brazier. A narrow bed with a perfectly folded blanket. A plain desk — not decorative, but finely maintained. A wall shelf of tactical scrolls and wind current charts. Mounted above the bed is a spiral-shaped symbol. The wind chimes outside his door have no silencing cloth. They hum constantly, as if he wants the wind to listen.

list.li: Several open scrolls detailing aerial patrol patterns, response formations, and internal notes on Society members.
Insight DC 12: The notes are precise, surgical — like a man profiling everyone around him.
A written assessment on Savra, partially covered by a duty roster:

p.i: “Loyal in ritual. Unproven in conviction. Keeps her emotions hidden — likely protecting someone. May need to be tested.”

text.p: Another note on Thurl, unflattering:

p.i: “Charisma ≠ strength. The wind will abandon him when it sees his weakness.”

text.p: Tucked in a false bottom beneath his drawer (Investigation DC 13) is a small personal copy of “The Four Winds Manifest” — a core cult text.

list.li: Several passages are underlined in sharp, angular strokes:

p.i: “Those who breathe the sky owe no loyalty to stone.”
“The weak submit to gravity. The worthy rise.”

list.li: Religion DC 14: This is advanced air cult doctrine — not meant for initiates. Tywin is not just a loyalist — he is a zealot.
A ritual knife with a feathered hilt, stored with care.
A wooden emblem of Yan-C-Bin’s spiral inlaid with silver threads — this isn’t worship. It’s allegiance.

text.p: In the back of a tactical log is a cold observation, written as if for a superior:

p.i: “Should Savra resist, she can be made an example. If she submits, she can still serve.”

text.p: This could be especially chilling if Eren finds it.

list.li: Arcana/Religion DC 12: The spiral symbol is an elemental glyph — stylized to look harmless, but ancient and dangerous in origin.
Insight DC 14: Tywin views most people as assets or liabilities. Even Thurl is a stepping stone.
Passive Perception 14+: The wind near the door vibrates oddly — like it’s listening.

text.p: This room is dim, lit only by the glow of filtered sunlight through a narrow slit window. Two beds sit on opposite ends of the space — both neatly made, but one with military precision, the other merely tidy. Between them, a shared desk holds an oil lamp, a few training manuals, and a half-drunk tin cup of cold herbal tea. A faint scent of sweat, steel oil, and incense clings to the air. Boots are lined at the base of each bed — one pair scuffed and patched, the other polished to a mirror finish.
Knight Aerlan – A model soldier, utterly devoted to the cult and its hierarchy
Initiate Vel – Newer to the Spire, quietly uncertain, hiding his doubts

list.li: A small handwritten note tucked under a manual (Investigation DC 12): “You’re not supposed to feel the wind watching. But I do. Every night. It’s wrong.”
Religion DC 13: Indicates exposure to an elemental ritual — likely the Wind Meditation Chamber — gone badly.

text.p: Vel’s Footlocker (Investigation DC 13)
Contains:

list.li: A Lathander prayer charm wrapped in cloth
A folded note written in Common, unsigned:

p.i: “If you can read this and still sleep soundly, you don’t belong here.”

list.li: Insight DC 12: Vel fears being found out. He’s still in — for now — but close to breaking.

text.p: Aerlan’s Side

list.li: Meticulously aligned uniform, dagger laid above the pillow
Beneath his bed (Perception DC 13): A small feather carved from bone, tied with pale blue thread — a personal cult token

text.p: This room feels heavier. Both beds are sharply made. The air is slightly chill, and a tall steel-framed mirror stands propped between the footlockers. Someone has carved a spiral pattern into the wood near the door — worn down, as if traced often by nervous fingers. On the desk: a copy of The Path of the Hollow Sky, opened to a dog-eared page.
Knight Gavik – A firm believer in the “cleansing” purpose of the cult
Knight Halra – More fanatical, ritual-oriented, and a watcher of Savra
Cult Text on Desk
Annotated with phrases like:
Arcana or Religion DC 14: These phrases are adapted cult mantras, not found in official Feathergale code. They echo Yan-C-Bin worship.

list.li: A list of “Recruit Evaluation Notes” — not official
Savra: “Emotionally compromised.”
Eren: “Unknown. Dangerous if she wavers.”
A crude drawing of a knight falling from a spire into clouds — ritual symbolism
A small velvet pouch containing silver powder and a carved ivory feather — components for a minor air ritual
A folded piece of paper tucked inside: “When the wind calls her name, she will rise or she will break.”

text.p: If the PCs linger here:

list.li: They may hear boots in the hall — a knight passing by or checking on them.
Vel might later seek one of them out, whispering: “If you feel wrong about all this… trust that. Just don’t show it.”

text.p: Savra had proudly led you into this space before — but left unsaid were the details you now notice upon closer inspection. The Great Hall spans half the tower’s width. Massive arched windows flood the chamber with light, and high on the walls, colorful tapestries depict aerial battles between knights on hippogriffs, dragons, and other sky creatures. Mounted high above the windows, the preserved heads of griffons, wyverns, manticores, and owlbears leer silently down at the long, curved feasting table set between twin hearths. The air smells faintly of spiced wine and old leather. Everything shines — polished marble, gleaming goblets, golden candelabras — but it’s all too... sterile. No scuff marks, no minor damage from rowdy banquets or history. It feels like a set piece.
Tapestries: Hidden Story in the Art
Perception DC 13: One tapestry shows a knight not fighting a dragon — but saluting it, the dragon’s body ringed by swirling clouds. This is no victory. It’s an offering.
History DC 14: The depicted “dragons” are actually drakes — much smaller, common, not legendary threats. The Feathergale Society exaggerates their conquests.
Religion DC 13 (if studying symbols): The swirling clouds around the dragon bear faint air elemental glyphs worked into the embroidery — not artistic flourishes, but ritualistic.
Mounted Beast Heads: Strange Details
Nature DC 12: The manticore mounted above the southern hearth has broken wing joints — suggesting it was captured alive and tortured rather than hunted cleanly.
Investigation DC 14 (studying mounts): Several heads have small iron bolts still embedded deep in bone — like the creatures were restrained, not just killed.
Arcana DC 14 (optional magic detection): The manticores and griffons have traces of binding magic residue — typical for creatures forced into ritual sacrifice.
Feasting Table: Symbolism Hidden in Plain Sight

The long feasting table, if seen from above (Pinnacle, higher level, or minor flight magic), forms a spiral feather shape — the Society’s sigil, but laid out in elemental spiral logic (Air cult structure).
Perception DC 12 (walking the length of the table):
Subtle carvings at the center leg posts: “The breath is taken, the burden lifted.”
Religion DC 15: This is a modified funerary phrase — but altered for sacrificial rites to the Prince of Evil Air.

If a PC lingers too long studying the beast heads or art: A knight casually approaches, arms folded: “Beautiful, aren’t they? Every beast a reminder that the strong belong above… and the others feed the wind.”
A Wyndwyrd (musician) tuning a harp comments nervously: “All this glory… you’d almost think they didn’t lose anything.”
Simply studying the hall carefully: No immediate suspicion.
Touching the tapestries, mounts, or hidden carvings: +1 Suspicion if observed by a knight.
Asking direct, pointed questions about the trophies or rituals: +1 Suspicion depending on phrasing.

p.b: Key Player Takeaways if They Explore Well:

text.p: Feathergale Society's victories are half-truths at best.
Air cult symbols and rites are baked into the very structure of their celebrations.
Captivity and sacrifice have been part of their legacy — not just battle.

The guest quarters occupy the western curve of the Spire’s second floor, following the natural outer wall of the tower. Each room is identical in layout — symmetrical, efficient, and without unnecessary decoration.
Inside, you find:

list.li: Two twin-sized beds, each tucked against the gently curving stone wall, beds dressed in crisp white linens embroidered with a single silver feather at the foot.
Two writing desks, simple but finely made, positioned between the beds beneath a narrow window slit that lets the constant breeze pass through.
Two tall wardrobes, one standing beside each bed, carved lightly with spiraling feather patterns.
Two nightstands, each set with a small unlit oil lamp and a neatly folded cloth napkin.
A shared water basin of smooth, pale stone sits between the two beds, set into a low stand.

text.p: The stone floor is covered by a single circular rug, its pattern resembling a stylized wind current spiraling outward from the center. The air smells faintly of lavender and rain — clean, cool, almost unnaturally pure. There are no locks on the doors from the outside. Only simple sliding latches on the inside, offering a modest sense of privacy.
Location: Beneath one pillow
Discovery: Perception DC 12 while checking beds or nightstands
Item: A small woven feather charm, tucked under a pillow.
Knowledge Checks:
Arcana DC 13: Minor enchantment, used in dream induction rituals common among Air cultists.
Insight DC 12: Intended to influence sleeping minds — either soothe or manipulate.
Subtle hint that guests are being "prepared" even while resting.
Location: Stuffed behind a wardrobe plank
Discovery: Investigation DC 13 while searching wardrobes
Item: A torn, faded note, handwritten in Common.
Content: "They smile when they bind you. The Queen watches when you dream. Speak nothing but gratitude, or the sky will hear."
Knowledge Checks:
Religion DC 14: "The Queen" is Aerisi Kalinoth — revered as a divine or semi-divine figure by Air cultists.
Insight DC 12: Someone trapped here once warned future guests.
Foreshadows deeper cult manipulation happening within the Spire.
Location: On the underside of a nightstand drawer
Discovery: Investigation DC 14 while searching furniture
Item: A small stitched square of cloth, stuck to the underside.
Details:
It’s an embroidery of a spiral feather glyph.
Close inspection reveals four faint elemental symbols — air is prominent, others faded.
Knowledge Checks:
Arcana DC 14: It’s a simplified air cult symbol, used for marking places of ritual influence.
This was probably a "blessing" given by a knight or attendant during room preparation.
Location: Inside the shared stone basin, visible if dried or emptied Discovery: Perception DC 13 (if inspecting the basin closely)
Details: Tiny spiral carvings around the drain hole — deliberate, forming a pattern.
Knowledge Checks:
Arcana DC 13: It’s a minor ritual sigil, meant to purify or cleanse minds through proximity to air or water.
The very water they wash with carries ritual significance — a light form of indoctrination.
text.h: Secret Message Hidden in Guest Quarters
text.p: Location: Room 2 (The One with the Faded Welcome Note)
The faded note about "speaking only gratitude" hints this room was used before — by someone who understood something very wrong about the Spire.
How It’s Hidden:
Discovery Method:
After moving the wardrobe and searching behind it (already Investigation DC 13 for the first note)...
If they keep searching carefully or specifically look for more signs (say they pry into a crack or tap on the stonework):
Second Investigation Check (DC 15) or Perception DC 17
(This second check should feel like "digging deeper" — reward thoroughness.)
The Secret Message (Scratched Deep into Stone Behind the Wardrobe)
It's crude, scratched into the stone by a nail, claw, or knife point:

p.i: “The sky speaks lies. The Queen weeps poison. The breath you trust will betray you. Flee before the winds claim your name.”

text.p: Interpreting the Message:
Insight DC 12: The writer was terrified, but lucid — this is not rambling madness. It’s a warning.
Religion or Arcana DC 14: The "Queen" is almost certainly Aerisi Kalinoth.
History DC 13 (if cross-referencing "Queen" references): Aerisi is not just a cult leader — she is a self-proclaimed elemental monarch, tied to the Prince of Evil Air.
Impact on Players:
Subtle unease escalates.
Now it’s no longer about weird hospitality — it’s dangerous mind control and a worshipped entity.
Optional consequence:
If they mention finding this message to any Spire members (especially Tywin or loyalists), immediate +2 suspicion.
Optional bonus for clever players:
If they use magic (like Comprehend Languages or Detect Magic) while reading the message, they might notice:
The wall behind the scratch glows faintly with old binding magic residue — implying someone who resisted an indoctrination ritual once fought here.
Narrative Description:

Passing beneath the massive outer gates, you step into a 45-foot-long hall of gleaming white stone. The ceiling arches high above you, soaring into a smooth, domed vault from which a giant eagle carving hangs, suspended by thick iron chains. The eagle is crafted from a single massive timber, its wings of polished steel tucked tightly against its sides. Its steel head shines dully in the filtered sunlight from narrow slits high along the walls. At the far end of the hall stand two massive bronze doors, each over 12 feet tall, engraved with stylized feather motifs that seem to ripple in the stone when caught by the shifting light. The walls are smooth, almost unnaturally clean — no banners, no visible cracks, no dust. Only the subtle spiral motifs worked into the stonework hint at the Society’s obsession with the currents of air. A faint, ever-present breeze moves through the hall, lifting cloaks and hair — though no draft can be felt from the outside.

list.li: Perception DC 12: The eagle's talons are clenched, not posed gracefully — it’s ready to strike downward, not simply soar.
Insight DC 13: The eagle’s design is more predatory than protective — it speaks of dominance, not guardianship.
Arcana DC 13 (if inspected carefully): The chains and eagle are lightly warded — not just to hold the weight, but to allow it to be magically dropped if needed (defensive or sacrificial use).
History DC 12: The bronze doors' feather motifs match ancient elemental iconography, particularly the cults who revered air spirits — not just a noble house crest.

text.p: Narrative Description: (Southwest Corner, Ground Floor)
The entrance to the Armory lies beyond a thick-set wooden door banded with black iron, tucked into the southwest corner just off the grand front hall.
A worn brass plate above the door reads:
The door is closed at all times and kept locked — only officers like Tywin Terrorwind or a quartermaster have access.
The moment you approach, the air changes — colder, sharper, as if even the stones here remember steel.
Lock Quality: Good; DC 17 with thieves' tools to pick without magic.
Alternative Entry:
Successful Deception or Persuasion DC 16 on a knight to bluff temporary access.
Stealth DC 15 during heavy activity (e.g., before or after feasts).
The armory is a compact, efficient chamber designed for speed rather than spectacle:

list.li: Racks of longspears, lances, crossbows, and windrider saddles.
Steel helms and half-plate armor polished to a mirror sheen, etched with spiral feather crests.
At the far end, an ornate locked cabinet — clearly more valuable contents inside.

text.p: Feathergale Air Cult Robes

list.li: White and silver, embroidered with swirling glyphs not seen in official knight uniforms.

text.p: Storm-forged Spears

list.li: Charged with faint elemental air magic (residual, non-combat effects unless awakened).

text.p: Scroll of the Queen’s Blessing

list.li: Invocation prayer intended to bind or sacrifice captives to the Air Prince Yan-C-Bin.

text.p: Written Orders:

list.li: Hand-signed "By Aerisi Kalinoth’s Breath" — commanding Thurl to monitor the Sacred Stone Monastery and prepare initiates for ascension rites.

text.p: Narrative Description:

Past the bustle of the kitchens and the guarded armory, a plain wooden door leads to the Spire’s southern curve, where the warmth of the hearth fades and the wind grows sharper in the stones. Here, carved into the outer wall of the tower, lies the Initiate Dormitory — the living quarters for the Spire’s lowest ranks. The room is stark and symmetrical, built for function without comfort:

list.li: Four heavy wooden bunks line the curve of the wall, each bunk holding two stacked beds — one atop the other.
Each bunk shares a large, scarred wooden chest at its foot — battered but serviceable.
The beds are covered in plain white linens, no personal effects, no color beyond the occasional fraying edge.
From the ceiling, steel feather charms hang on thin chains, aligned directly above each bunk — their subtle sway always toward the room’s center.

text.p: The stone floor bears no carpet or padding — only faint scratches where boots have scuffed in and out, day after day. At the far side, narrow vents carved into the wall let in the constant whistling breath of the outside air — and with it, faint sounds almost like chanting, impossible to place. There is no fire here. No warmth. Only the wind and the expectation of silence.
Narrative Description: Eastern Side

A bright, airy room occupies the entire eastern quarter of the Spire's ground floor. Sunlight pours through tall, narrow windows, illuminating a sprawling labyrinth of raised stone planters arranged in spiraling patterns across the chamber. Flowers and shrubs of many colors and shapes grow here, cultivated with careful attention. Between the planters, narrow stone paths twist and wind like currents of air, leading deeper into the greenery. Overhead, dozens of spidery red and purple plants dangle from suspended baskets, some swaying gently despite the stillness of the air. Amid the lush growth, several robed figures move in slow, deliberate paths. The caretakers carry simple copper watering cans, tending to the plants in total silence — their faces calm, but their movements mechanical. Occasionally, one figure pauses — not to admire the beauty, but as if listening to something beyond the breeze, unseen and unheard. At the center of the solarium stands a small fountain, shaped like a stylized feather, from which clear water trickles softly into a shallow basin. The smells are fresh and vibrant — damp earth, sweet blooms — but lingered within is a faint, sharp trace of something metallic and bitter, just beyond clear recognition. Though the space is bathed in light and life, the longer you remain, the more it feels less like a garden... and more like a nursery — not for plants, but for obedience.

list.li: Nature DC 12: Many plants are non-native to the Dessarin Valley — some require climates closer to elemental planes.
Arcana DC 13: Some vines and hanging plants show reactive movement toward heat and sound — enchanted for subtle sensory rituals.
Insight DC 13: The spiral arrangement of the planters mirrors the wind spiral glyph — a signature of Air cult influence.
Perception DC 12: The water's reflection shows clouds swirling unnaturally, even on a clear day.
Investigation DC 14: Scratched on the base of the feather basin: “Only the breathless rise.”
Religion DC 14: This phrasing is linked to ritual sacrifice by suffocation — common among extreme air cult sects.
Passive Observation: They do not speak or interact unless interrupted.
Insight DC 12: Their movements suggest rote repetition — possibly spell-conditioned or indoctrinated behavior.
Perception DC 14: Beneath one attendant’s sleeve, you glimpse a spiral glyph branded or tattooed onto the skin.
