Arcana DC 13: Some of the suspended spidery plants are ritual-sensitive flora — they react to magical auras and mental states nearby, used historically in air ritual auguries.
Nature DC 13: These plants usually only grow in high-wind, planar-touched regions — unnatural here.

text.p: Narrative Description: North-Northwest

Tucked into the north-northwestern curve of the Spire’s base floor, a pair of heavy oak doors — their surfaces carved with swirling feather motifs — lead into a circular library chamber. Inside, the room is cool and shadowed, lit by slender windows set high along the outer wall and by tall, slender oil lamps spaced evenly around the space. Bookshelves rise almost to the domed ceiling, packed with well-kept tomes, rolled maps, loose scrolls, and bound journals. At the center of the room, a circular table holds an array of charts, navigational tools, and a polished celestial globe, depicting stars and shifting cloud patterns. The scent of old parchment, leather, and ink saturates the air — mingling with the faint, sharp smell of ozone. Everything appears orderly — pristine — but a closer look reveals subtle gaps on the shelves where books have been removed. Some of the open spaces bear faint marks of symbols carved into the wood, now hurriedly sanded over.

list.li: History DC 12: Many volumes focus on aerial navigation, weather patterns, wind currents, and chivalric histories.
Investigation DC 13 (searching missing spaces): You notice subtle carving remnants in the wood — faint spiral glyphs, often associated with elemental air rituals.
Insight DC 13: Large historical events — floods, storms, disappearances in the valley — are downplayed or omitted in surviving records.
Perception DC 13: A rolled map of the Dessarin Valley has strange markings near the Sacred Stone Monastery — spiral cloud symbols not explained in any key.
Arcana DC 14: Those spiral markings match ritual sites used by elemental cults to anchor planar energy.

text.p: A beautiful, ancient globe showing the night sky, but with a strange twist:

list.li: Arcana DC 14 or Investigation DC 14:Some of the constellations are altered — subtly reshaped into spiral patterns around an unseen central point.
Insight DC 13: This suggests a religious reinterpretation — turning the natural world into symbols of ascension and domination.

text.p: Investigation DC 15 (while searching high shelves or behind scroll racks):
Hidden behind a row of fake "Weather Studies" volumes:

list.li: A leather-bound book with no title.
Inside: a handwritten manifesto titled "Breath Beyond Stone" — a treatise on rejecting the material world and ascending through elemental sacrifice.
Investigation 20: Inside the leather-bound book, scrawled in tight, neat script:

p.i: “When the stone-bound are broken and the breathless are lifted, the faithful shall gather at the Throne of Wind — where the Howling Crown is set above all. Beneath the roots of the world, where light forgets its name, the Queen reigns eternal. There shall the Last Breath be taken, and the Unworthy hurled into the void below. Only the hollow and the willing shall soar.”

text.p: Religion DC 14: The writer praises Yan-C-Bin, not as a god, but as a force of "pure cleansing."

Large archways open to the outside air along the cliff face — wide enough for beasts to launch into the sky, yet designed so that the strong winds rarely whip into the stable itself.Inside, stone stalls line the perimeter, each holding a hippogriff, giant vulture, or other aerial steed. The creatures stir and shift as you enter — not with fear, but with a tense, expectant energy. The smell of animal musk, oiled leather, and damp stone saturates the chamber. In the center of the stables lies a low, circular platform, marked with a spiraling feather glyph — used for mount ceremonies, blessings, and other purposes. Simple wooden racks hold saddles, bridles, and banners embroidered with the Feathergale spiral. A few robed attendants quietly tend to the beasts, feeding them and brushing their coats without speaking. The constant sound of distant wind echoes through the open archways, blending with the occasional low screech of a restless mount.

list.li: Nature DC 12: The hippogriffs and vultures bear ritual spiral brands under their manes or wing joints.
Insight DC 13:These creatures are not merely trained — they have been ritually bonded to the Feathergale knights through pain and magical coercion.
Perception DC 13 (observing markings): The spiral design incorporates elemental air glyphs.
Arcana DC 14: The platform is a low-grade ritual anchor — used to bless, bind, or sacrifice flying beasts to enhance their "loyalty" through air elemental magic.

text.p: Saddles and bridles include feather motifs worked into the leather.

list.li: Investigation DC 12: Hidden inside a saddle pouch: a small scroll describing the Windbound Rite — a ceremony to force obedience on unwilling mounts and initiates alike.
Religion DC 13: This rite is not normal training — it involves oaths sworn to elemental spirits, not just to the Society or Thurl.
Perception DC 12 (watching the wind currents): The outer arches are marked subtly with binding glyphs, controlling the air flow to make launches easier — or force a rider to fall, if so directed.
Arcana DC 13: These glyphs can subtly sabotage flight if activated during a "trial."

text.p: Initial Narrative Description:

As the sun tilts toward the horizon, golden light floods the Great Hall through tall arched windows, casting long, soft shadows across the feather-patterned tapestries and the polished marble floor. The long, curved feasting table is now fully set — plates of roasted meats, baked breads, honeyed fruits, and flagons of crisp white wine gleam under the light of silver candelabras. Feathergale Knights — resplendent in their white and silver attire — stand behind high-backed chairs, waiting until Thurl Merosska himself enters, adorned in flowing feathered cloak and polished armor. He raises a goblet high, voice carrying easily over the soft clatter of dishes:
text.frame: “To guests of honor — and to the boundless skies that cradle us all! May you rise higher than the stones below!”
text.p: He gestures warmly for the party and the Wyndwyrds (the musicians) to join the meal. Savra, positioned near Thurl but not directly at his side, watches the proceedings with careful, measured expressions. Tywin Terrorwind, standing rigid two seats down, eyes everyone coldly — especially the party. The Wyndwyrds begin playing a soft, lilting melody in the background, giving the entire feast an air of easy celebration:
Players are encouraged to:
Share backstories
Share recent adventures
Share motives (in part or fully)
Telling stories = totally safe.
Mentioning observations (strange cult behavior, suspicions about the tower, glyphs, etc.) = raises minor alarms.
If players hint at investigations or cult suspicions:

list.li: Insight Check (Passive DC 12): Knights start trading glances.
+1 suspicion if specific rituals, glyphs, or secret rooms are mentioned openly.

text.p: Just as the meal hits its comfortable middle — wine flowing, laughter rising:
A Feathergale Knight bursts into the hall, breathing hard, helmet tucked under one arm.

p.i: “Commander Merosska!” he calls, saluting sharply. “Sighting confirmed — the beast circles Sighing Valley again! The manticore returns!”

text.p: The hall immediately quiets. Knights lean forward in excitement — more hungry for glory than concerned.
Thurl rises slowly, smiling like a king at court:

p.i: “Fortune rides the winds tonight. A rare hunt calls us to action, my friends — and what better entertainment for our honored guests?”

text.p: He raises his goblet toward the party:

p.i: “A bounty to the brave: My ring and 500 gold pieces to the one who brings the beast’s head before me!”

text.p: The knights erupt in cheers, slapping the table and calling for arms.Thurl then turns directly to the party:

p.i: “Join us, if you have the courage. Ride the skies with us... or watch from below.”

text.p: The Great Hall buzzes with anticipation after the knight’s urgent report, but Thurl Merosska swiftly silences it with a single raised hand.
"With me," he says, his voice carrying clearly.
Flanked by Tywin Terrorwind and Savra Belabranta, Thurl leads the party to the far side of the hall, where a wide spiral staircase of smooth, pale stone winds downward into the depths of the tower.
The air cools noticeably as you descend, the noise of the feast above replaced by the steady echoes of your own footfalls.
The stairwell is open at the center, spiraling elegantly around a hollow shaft that plunges downward, vanishing into shadow.

After a few turns, the stairs deposit you onto the Stable Level — a broad stone cavern carved directly into the cliff face, where hippogriffs and giant vultures shift restlessly in their stalls, the scent of hay and damp stone thick in the air.
The mounts regard you with intelligent, wary eyes, but no saddles are prepared.
This hunt will be on foot.
Thurl strides across the stables without pause.
At the far side, set into the outer curve of the tower, another narrow spiral stair winds downward — this time hugging the exterior cliff, open to the night air.
The wind rises as you step onto the outer stair, tugging at cloaks and hair.
The stone beneath your feet is rougher here, less polished — built for utility rather than grandeur.
With each step downward, the valley below grows closer: an endless undulating sea of dark grasses, broken stones, and twisted trees.
The setting sun has nearly vanished beyond the western horizon, leaving the world painted in deep blue and violet.
At the base of the Spire, the stairs terminate on a wide stone platform at ground level.
Before you stretch two distinct trails:

list.li: To the left, a narrow, broken path winding through sharp rocks and jagged cliffs — known as the Dead Rocks Path.
To the right, a wider trail following the course of a slow, silvery river — the River Path.

text.p: Somewhere beyond sight, a deep, rumbling roar rolls across the hills, shaking loose stones underfoot.
The manticore is near.
Thurl turns, his feathered cloak snapping in the rising wind:
"Choose your course, bold hunters. The skies watch — and they remember the worthy."
He says no more, leaving the decision in your hands.
Dead rocks
Knifepoint Gully(Optional)
North Howling Plateau
Lost River Entry
Griffon Roost(Optional)
South Howling Plateau
Lost River Exit
Aarakocra Camp (Optional)
Manticore Lair

The trail narrows sharply as it twists through a chaos of broken stone and jagged crags. The wind howls between the rocks, carrying the dry, metallic scent of old blood. Up ahead, a grim sight unfolds: Perched atop a boulder streaked with dark stains, a giant vulture tears lazily at a heap of rotting flesh and shattered bones. The creature's bald, crimson-streaked head jerks up occasionally, scanning the skies — wary, but not fearful. Circling above, six blood hawks ride the updrafts, their cries sharp and eager. They dive low when anything stirs among the rocks but keep distance for now, waiting for their chance. The ground is littered with remains: broken weapons, scraps of cloth, and gnawed bones cracked by powerful beaks. The stench of death hangs heavy here — days old, baked into the stones by sun and wind.

list.li: DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation): The bones are humanoid — not beasts or animals.

If succeeded by 5+ (DC 20 Investigation): You find old rusty stains — dried blood pools, shattered bone fragments — evidence that many deaths have occurred here over time. These weren't isolated kills — this spot is a graveyard.

tr.td: Feeds quietly; attacks only if provoked (attacked, approached too closely)
Circle overhead; attack any living creature (including players) if they approach the kill too closely or disturb the vulture

p.b: Closing Narrative (after DC 14 Perception Check Success):

text.p: As you pick your way through the broken stones beyond Dead Rocks, the shifting wind briefly lifts a screen of dust and pale brush. Through the haze, you glimpse a narrow fissure opening in the canyon wall — almost invisible unless viewed from just the right angle. The entrance is tight and uneven, barely wide enough for a person to slip through single-file. Pale, twisted shrubs choke the narrow path beyond, their skeletal branches whispering against one another as a swift breeze snakes through the fissure. The wind is colder here, carrying a thin, dry scent like old bones. At the far end, where the gully deepens into shadow, a dark, jagged crevice looms — a tear in the rock that seems almost to breathe with the rhythm of the wind. The main trail winds onward into the hills, broader and more predictable. But this hidden route — this Knifepoint Gully — offers a faster, riskier way forward... if you dare.

p.b: Closing Narrative (after DC 14 Perception Check fail):

text.p: The wind grows stronger as you leave the grisly scene behind, tugging at your cloaks and whispering through the broken stones. The trail presses onward into the teeth of the hills — winding upward between jagged crags and crumbling ledges. Dust rises with every step, and the rocky terrain forces you to move in single file, always scanning the cliffs above for danger. Around you, the shadows lengthen as the last light of day fades into deep violet. The land grows harsher, more empty — as if even the vultures and blood hawks know better than to linger too long. There is only the trail ahead... and the distant, rumbling roar that still echoes somewhere beyond the hills.

As you push deeper through the narrow gully, the pale brush gives way to bare, cracked stone. The wind sharpens into a cutting force, whistling between the narrow walls as if in warning. Then the ground falls away. Before you, an enormous chasm splits the earth — an endless black void that seems to drink the scant light. Far below, you can hear only silence... the sound of the earth itself holding its breath. A crude, narrow stairway clings precariously to the cliffside, twisting wildly in mad spirals around jagged outcroppings. The path is barely more than loose rock, chiseled steps, and the occasional ancient rope handhold — a treacherous descent that would spill the unwary into the abyss below. The very sight of it draws a primal shiver — this was never meant for casual travel. Just as the oppressive awe settles over you, movement flickers at the edge of vision. But before you can move closer, figures emerge from the shadows above. Two robed humans, their pale gray mantles marked with faint spiral glyphs, descend lightly to block your path. The air around them bends and ripples, like heat shimmering off desert stone — the mark of air magic, tightly leashed and waiting. One raises a hand, palm outward in warning, his voice clipped and emotionless:

A moment later, the scrape of boots against stone draws your eye upward. Tywin Terrorwind steps onto the ledge above, his feathered cloak snapping sharply in the mounting wind. He regards you with narrowed eyes, voice cold and final:

p.i: "This path leads only to places meant for the ascended. There is no quarry for you here."

text.p: His gaze lingers for a heartbeat — heavy with silent threat — before he gestures sharply back toward the main trail.

list.li: If questioned about the chasm, Tywin answers with cool efficiency:

p.i: "A manticore does not nest in stone tombs. It flies where prey is plentiful."

list.li: If pressed further, his patience thins:

p.i: "The wind does not waste time with idle chatter. Neither should you."

text.p: The Hurricanes stand unmoving, silent guardians of the forbidden descent.
The message is unmistakable: leave, or be forced to leave.

The trail winds down from the broken crags, the rocks underfoot loosening and slipping with each step. Ahead, the canyon opens into a vast, high plateau — its stone surface bleached pale by endless sun and wind. You stand now on the northern edge of the plateau, looking down a gradual rocky slope toward a shallow valley where the river cuts a silver thread through the canyon floor. The plateau itself rises sharply beyond the river, a sheer wall of rock that dominates the landscape. Even from here, you can see the jagged cliffs and broken columns of stone that jut up like ancient, crumbling teeth. The wind here is a living thing. It keens and moans across the rocks, its pitch shifting eerily with every gust — rising into a wail, then falling into a guttural whisper. Loose stones rattle across the ground, clicking like bones underfoot. Far above, circling high on the air currents, you glimpse a few dark shapes — hawks, perhaps... or something larger. Just as you near the halfway point down the slope, a sharp, tearing cry cuts across the moaning wind. From the high cliffs above, two dark shapes peel away from the rocks — Preytons — their twisted antlers catching the last rays of the dying sun, their leathery wings beating madly against the gusts. Their cries rise and fall unnaturally, echoing off the stone like mocking laughter. With a sudden lurch of movement, they dive, angling straight toward you with savage hunger gleaming in their hollow, animal eyes.

list.li: Antlers are angular, twisted shapes that seem almost wrong
Broad, leathery wings beat the thinning air with heavy strokes,
Their bodies bear the muscular build of great stags — long-limbed and powerful — but their heads are a nightmare:
elongated skulls crowned with broken, jagged antlers, and jaws stretched too wide in a mockery of a hunter's snarl.
Curved talons rake against the stone — more bird than beast, sharpened for rending as much as running.
Their cries — a shrieking blend of bird and beast — shatter the wind’s howl, clawing at your ears and stirring some ancient, primal dread.

linklist.link: Encounter: Episode#1.20.10 North Howling Plateau Encounter

text.p: The river sweeps close against the eastern canyon wall, its current rushing fast over pale stone and broken reeds. To the west, rocky spires and wild brush grow dense, their tangled roots clawing through the dry soil. The wind shifts uneasily here, pushing and pulling at the brush like unseen hands. As you move cautiously along the trail, something catches your eye:

list.li: Torn scraps of cloth snagged on the low shrubs.
A battered waterskin lying half-buried in the dust.
And just beyond a cluster of spires, half hidden beneath scattered rocks... a body.

text.p: The figure lies crumpled awkwardly, clothing tattered, limbs twisted in death.The wind keens softly through the canyon as you approach.

p.b: Important Details Found on the Body:

list.li: Torn Emblem: A spiral-shaped insignia partially burned into a leather scrap (Air Cult symbol, but disguised).
Crude Map Fragment:A torn piece of rough parchment showing rough landmarks: the river, dead rocks, and an ominous spiral marked deep in the hills (points toward Feathergale territory).
Scrawled Message (Optional Find): On the inside of a boot or tucked into a sleeve:

p.i: "They kneel to a queen crowned in storms. Flee before you are hollowed."

text.p: The river bends sharply again, the rush of water echoing strangely off the canyon walls. As you move forward, the scent of blood thickens in the air — iron-rich and sharp, carried on the keening wind. Just off the trail, half hidden among the rocks and brush, you find it: A pool of blood. Wide, still sticky, darkening the dust and stone. Scattered around it lie broken lances, a shredded white cloak marked with a silver spiral, and the splintered remains of fine saddles and riding tack — all equipment unmistakably belonging to Feathergale Knights. But there are no bodies. Only deep gouges in the ground, torn leather, and the signs of a violent struggle — and then, something large dragging its prize skyward.

tr.td: You find small white feathers caught on the rocks, and deep talon scores gouged into stone — unmistakable signs of a griffon attack.
The trail of blood and torn gear leaves you convinced it must be the manticore’s work — brutal, messy, savage.

p.b: Success Narrative (If Players Succeed the Check):

text.p: This was no manticore. A griffon — swift, territorial, and deadly — struck here, carrying its prey aloft.

Following the trail carefully, you spot it: a narrow, difficult track leading away from the river and up the canyon’s steep eastern cliffs. Above, silhouetted against the last light of the sky, you glimpse broken nests — huge tangled masses of branches and bone — perched precariously along the ridge.

p.b: Tywin's Arrival (if they fail the check):

text.p: As the players draw conclusions — or linger too long — a sharp gust of wind heralds the arrival of a figure from above. Tywin Terrorwind, astride a hippogriff, descends heavily nearby, his feathered cloak snapping in the gale. His face is a mask of cold disapproval.Landing heavily, Tywin swings down from his mount and strides toward you, boots crunching through the dust and blood. His voice cuts through the swirling wind:

p.i: "The beast is bold tonight. To kill knights of the Spire..."
"You see now why the hunt must end swiftly."

text.p: If questioned or pressed:

p.i: "Manticore talons tear flesh from bone. You have the proof at your feet."
"Hesitation will only claim more of us."

text.p: He leaves no room for argument — redirecting you toward the hunt with heavy, unspoken authority.

The trail grows thinner and rougher as you ascend the canyon wall. At first it’s a mere animal path — broken stones, crumbling handholds — then it disappears entirely into steep, exposed rock. You are forced to climb, fingers scraping for cracks and ledges, the river far below a silver ribbon through the dusty landscape. The wind presses against you as you climb, rising in fitful gusts that tug at cloaks and weapons. Loose stones occasionally clatter away towards the lower level.
(Climb Mechanics Note: Athletics checks DC 5 per 30 feet; 60–80 feet total climb; failure risks falling 10–20 feet unless caught.)
After what feels like an hour compressed into minutes, you reach the top — a narrow rocky shelf leading to a dark, low entrance carved into the cliff face.

The air grows thick and musky as you approach the cave. The heavy stench of animal musk, damp earth, and rotting straw hangs in the air like a wet cloth. It fills your nostrils, clinging to your skin and armor. Inside, the cave walls are rough, streaked with old claw marks and feather tufts. A massive nest of straw, twigs, and bones follows the gentle curvature of the stone — sprawling across much of the cavern floor. Cracked bones — some animal, some perhaps humanoid — litter the edges of the nest. Near the center of the nest, partially hidden under layers of straw and feathers, you spot them: Two griffon eggs — each roughly the size of a small keg, their shells marbled white and gold. They are motionless, but the faint warmth of the air and the care of the nest suggests they are viable, still waiting to hatch.The space hums faintly with the sound of shifting feathers and low, rhythmic breathing. Something very large is inside — though for now, it remains hidden by the curve of the cave wall.

list.li: Stealth DC 13 Approach silently, possibly avoid immediate combat
Investigation DC 12 Identify humanoid remains or scavenged armor scraps (possible Air Cult prisoner gear)
Nature DC 14 Understand griffon territorial behavior — it will attack if threatened or if it senses intruders too close to the nest

text.p: Whether following the winding river trail or climbing down from the heights of the Griffon Roost, you eventually reach the southern face of the plateau. The landscape changes subtly here:

list.li: Low, twisted shrubs and tufts of coarse grass cling stubbornly to the rocky soil.
Patches of scraggly vegetation cluster around the base of broken stone outcroppings.
The river cuts through the canyon floor nearby, its waters dark and swift.

text.p: The plateau itself rises high, a broad, rocky shelf etched by ancient winds.

Above you, the wind keens and moans — its voice rising and falling with almost living emotion — shifting pitch with each gust as if the stone itself were singing in pain. The open expanse stretches before you — and the lack of cover is instantly unnerving.

As you move cautiously across the plateau, the howling wind plays tricks on your senses — distant echoes sound like footsteps, scattered rocks tumble like whispers. Then, suddenly: Two shrieking forms descend from the stone outcrops above — harpies, their wings battered and ragged, their mouths twisted into wicked grins as they screech over the wind. At the same moment, from the shadows of a nearby rocky hollow, two smaller shapes burst forth — stirges, hideous bloodsucking things with twitching wings and barbed proboscises. Drawn by the vibrations of your passage, the scavengers strike.

Descending from the battered winds of the Howling Plateau, the landscape shifts again. The river sweeps close against the canyon’s eastern wall, its waters darker now in the deepening twilight. To the south, the ground rises into rocky spires and tangled wild brush, casting long crooked shadows across the cracked earth. The wind here is heavier, sluggish, carrying the faint, bitter stench of rot and blood. As you make your way through the broken terrain, your path curves along the river’s edge — and that’s when you find it:

list.li: Deep gouges raked through the sandy soil.
Clumps of dark, matted fur caught on thorny brush.
Massive footprints, almost leonine but twisted — each step ending in long, wicked claw marks.

text.p: Near the base of one larger rock outcropping, a shattered carcass lies sprawled — the remains of some unlucky creature, its body half-consumed and torn open, the flesh ragged as if ripped by barbed teeth

list.li: Survival DC 12 Track the manticore's movements; determine direction (toward a nearby lair or deeper into the canyon).
Nature DC 13 Recognize the distinctive signs: this kill matches descriptions of manticore feeding behavior.
Investigation DC 12 Identify the claw marks and realize this was not a casual kill — it was territorial violence (the manticore is establishing dominance here).

text.p: As you circle a riverside you are lost under the trees and brush, Tywin’s presence — so constant before — fades behind you. A momentary lapse. The party is alone, without the watchful eye of the Feathergale Society for the first time since the Spire. And that's when you see them

Tucked into a depression along the ridge, shielded by pale brush and twisted shrubs, you spot movement. Five Aarakocra — tall, lean birdfolk with weathered plumage the color of stone and sand — watch you from within their hidden post. Their wings are bound close against their bodies, and their sharp eyes gleam with wary intelligence. Weapons are close at hand, but they make no aggressive moves. One, taller than the rest and wearing a necklace of woven bones and crystals, steps forward carefully. Their voice is a dry whisper, half lost in the moaning wind:

p.i: "You walk dangerous ground. Air, stone, and death twine here. The winds are no longer free."
"The canyon is poisoned. Corrupted. Forces of great evil stir beneath the stone and sky."

text.p: If the party shows interest in challenging this evil or even hints at distrust toward the Feathergale Society:

p.i: "We have seen the rituals. The blood offerings. Some still believe the sky can be cleansed... but others kneel to darker powers."

text.p: However, if asked directly about interfering if the party were captured:
The aarakocra grow silent — a heavy, uncomfortable pause. Then the elder speaker says, with finality:

p.i: "We do not intervene unless the sky itself cries out. You must choose your own currents."
"Should you fall... we cannot promise rescue."

text.p: The brush rustles sharply behind you. Before you can fully turn, the wind shifts — carrying the heavy wingbeats of a descending hippogriff. Tywin Terrorwind drops into view atop his mount, his feathered cloak whipping in the rising gusts. He reins in hard, dismounts in one smooth motion, and strides forward, boots grinding dust and pebbles underfoot. His sharp eyes scan the terrain — lingering a heartbeat too long on the ridge where the aarakocra hid — before settling on you. His voice is steady, but low and clipped:
"You strayed from the trail."
A pause — long enough for discomfort to set in — before he continues, tone sharpening:

p.i: "The trail you seek is close. The beast's lair lies ahead, where the river coils into broken stone."
"If it senses hesitation... it will strike first."

text.p: He says nothing of the deviation, makes no direct accusation.
But there is no warmth left in his voice — only expectation, and the threat of consequence.

list.li: DC 12 Insight: You sense he is suspicious — but unwilling to make an open accusation yet. He is watching for signs of weakness or deception.
If Players Offer an Excuse (e.g., "tracking the manticore," "following tracks"): Tywin nods slowly but without warmth.

text.p: "The prey will not wait for lost hunters. Stay focused." (He accepts the explanation outwardly — but increases his private suspicion.)

list.li: If Players Are Evasive or Nervous:

text.p: Tywin steps closer, voice tightening:

p.i: "The canyon swallows the foolish. I suggest you tread carefully, before you vanish from our sight for good."

list.li: If Players Push Back or Ask What’s Wrong:

text.p: Tywin’s eyes harden. His tone turns iron:

p.i: "We have been patient hosts. Loyal to the Spire. Loyal to the sky. Do not force us to choose between mercy and duty."

text.p: Following the river’s edge into a narrowing canyon, you find a deep natural cleft in the rock — dark, wet, and heavy with the scent of minerals and decay. At the mouth of the cave, a wide pool glistens under faint light. Fed by a natural spring deep beneath the stone, the water fills the center of the cavern, then spills outward into the river beyond. Above, long, crooked stalactites drip steadily, the rhythmic patter of water creating an eerie chorus that echoes through the hollow. At the heart of the pool rises a natural stone pillar, its surface slick with moss and mineral deposits. Half-submerged along the edges of the pool, you spot the crumbling remains of an old campsite:

list.li: Four battered crates sit cracked and half-flooded.
Moldy scraps of cloth cling to broken frames.
Rusted metal tools and splintered wood drift half-sunken along the edges.

text.p: The water is cold, the air damp — and the feeling that something watches from the darkness gnaws at the edges of your senses.

Beyond the pool, a narrow rocky passage slopes upward slightly — the air growing drier, warmer, and thicker with the musky stench of beast. The dripping echoes fade into deeper silence. Here, the ground turns rough, cracked by sharp stones and clawed earth. The second chamber opens wide — a natural dry basin, filled with scattered bones, claw marks gouged into the walls, and the foul, acrid stink of a predator’s den. This place belongs to something savage and territorial. At the far end of the dry chamber, tucked between two sharp stone spires, a massive form stirs — leathery wings flexing once, then settling heavily.
The Manticore.
Its golden eyes gleam in the low light — a creature of hatred and hunger, disturbed in its lair.

list.li: Stealth DC 13 Move quietly across the water’s edge to avoid alerting the Manticore too soon
Investigation DC 12 Identify the crates' contents (old supplies, broken weapons — no treasure, but signs of old adventurers)
Perception DC 14 Notice claw drag marks leading deeper into the drier tunnel

text.p: When the first Manticore (Alpha) drops to 50% hit points or lower, immediately describe:
The manticore rears up with a guttural roar — a sound that shakes dust from the cavern walls and sets the stagnant air trembling.
It’s not a battle cry.
It's a call.
Mechanics of the Roar:

list.li: No action required — happens immediately as part of taking damage to half health.
Echoing roar is heard through the caves and canyon outside.
If a second manticore exists nearby (your call based on balance), it begins flying toward the lair.
Arrival in 1d4 rounds — roll immediately.

text.p: The wounded manticore stumbles backward, bleeding heavily, wings tattered and breath ragged. You tighten your grip, ready to land the final blow — the kill within reach. But then — a rush of boots on stone — a shadow at the edge of your vision. Tywin Terrorwind bursts forward from the rocky entrance, moving with brutal precision. Before you can react, his blade flashes in a clean, practiced arc — slicing deep into the manticore’s exposed flank. With a final gurgling snarl, the beast collapses — dead at Tywin’s feet. Dust and blood settle around him in the silence that follows. Tywin stands tall, sword lowered but ready, the manticore’s corpse between you. His voice cuts through the cavern, calm but dripping with condescension:
He wipes the blade on the beast’s ruined hide and sheathes it with a sharp, practiced motion.
Thurl Merosska — Commander of the Feathergale Society — enters the cavern atop a striking hippogriff, dismounting smoothly.
Behind him strides Savra Belabranta, her expression unreadable but her armor pristine.
Thurl's gaze sweeps the scene — the fallen manticore, the battered party, Tywin standing tall — and a slow, approving smile touches his face.

p.i: "Well done, Tywin. A clean kill. The Spire is fortunate to have such swift blades among its champions."

text.p: Savra steps forward, her voice calm but firm:

p.i: "They all played their part. But it was Tywin’s hand that delivered the final strike."

text.p: There is no room for argument — no space left for your truth to take root. Your contributions are buried beneath the pageantry of rank and appearance. The victory has been taken from your hands — and the world will remember their version of events, not yours.

The canyon lies steeped in silence, painted in shadows and starlight. It is just past the eleventh bell, and the world has grown cold. The rocks radiate the heat of the day in low, sullen pulses, but the air is dry and sharp with nightfall. The only sound is the wind, thin and distant — like a breath held too long. The manticore’s body lies quiet behind you, and the moon casts fractured light through the jagged cliffs ahead. Near the entrance, the hippogriffs stand waiting, reins tied loosely to a stone ring. Their feathers shimmer faintly in the dimness. Tucked beneath one saddle strap is a folded parchment bearing the Feathergale seal — Thurl’s script, curt and exact: “Return when ready. The Spire awaits. — T.M.”
text.h: Secret GM Detail: Surveillance in the Shadows
text.p: Unknown to the party, Tywin and Thurl have not fully left. High above, perched among the upper canyon ridges under a natural overhang, two figures watch from the back of their hippogriffs, cloaks drawn tight against the wind. They observe the party’s movements — whether they return, hesitate, explore, or stray toward forbidden paths.
Mechanics:
Perception check DC 20 (disadvantage due to darkness) to spot a glint of armor or shifting silhouette high above.
If the party uses magic (e.g., detect magic or true seeing), you may allow them to catch a shadow of a presence — but still likely too far to identify.
Their Purpose:

list.li: To confirm the party’s loyalty or independence.
If the party enters Knifepoint Gully, Tywin will intercept and prevent the players from entering and will then escort them back to the spire
Tywin will add to his private suspicion dossier — the party’s fate is slowly being decided above their heads.

text.h: Optional DM Flavor for Subtle Suspicion (if you want to hint):
text.p: As the party prepares their next steps — mounting, walking, or wandering — you might add:
Somewhere above, a faint scraping of rock might be heard — just once.
Or the hippogriffs glance upward briefly, then look away.
But the night remains silent.
Nothing conclusive. Just enough to plant the seed: they’re not as alone as they think.

You follow the narrow ridge path cut into the canyon wall, moonlight tracing sharp lines along the stone. Ahead, between two low outcrops, lies a shallow depression — a hollow shadowed in brush and tumbled rock. This is where the Aarakocra had made their camp. But now, it is still. No voices. No movement. No wind-stirred feathers. Just cold silence.
Looking over the site:

list.li: You find light signs of haste:
An overturned fire ring.
A snapped bone wind chime hanging askew.
A half-buried pouch of dried food.

text.p: They didn’t pack. They didn’t clean.
They left fast — and likely by air.
Attempting to follow their trail:

list.li: You confirm it: there are no clear footprints, no path leading away.
But you notice bent shrubs, crushed feathers in certain spots, and an updraft channel along the ridge.

text.p: The wind here is stronger — it swirls in spirals near the ledges.

Putting it together, they likely took off from the eastern edge, where the land dips toward the norththern cliffs — somewhere in the direction of Knifepoint Gully, though no exact heading can be confirmed.
Studying the wind glyphs or environmental change:

list.li: Some of the wind glyphs still hum faintly. These were protective wards, and they’ve been consciously dismissed — not disrupted.

text.p: The air here was once defended. Now, it's exposed.

list.li: There’s a subtle pressure in the air moving toward the canyon’s deeper southern fork — like a natural flow of wind being redirected.

text.p: Something is disturbing the air currents beyond this ridge — something elemental.

The canyon narrows as you press forward. The wind thins — no longer howling, but breathing, like something alive. The air feels stale, like the wind here isn’t fresh but trapped, moving in loops between the stones. As the moon passes behind a drifting cloud, you spot it: A fissure in the rock wall, nearly hidden by brush — a narrow gully, hemmed by pale, wind-smoothed stone. The opening leads downward into a twisting depression, choked with ghost-pale shrubs and dust.

As you push deeper through the narrow gully, the pale brush gives way to bare, cracked stone. The wind sharpens into a cutting force, whistling between the narrow walls as if in warning. Then the ground falls away. Before you, an enormous chasm splits the earth — an endless black void that seems to drink the scant light. Far below, you can hear only silence... the sound of the earth itself holding its breath. A crude, narrow stairway clings precariously to the cliffside, twisting wildly in mad spirals around jagged outcroppings. The path is barely more than loose rock, chiseled steps, and the occasional ancient rope handhold — a treacherous descent that would spill the unwary into the abyss below. The very sight of it draws a primal shiver — this was never meant for casual travel. Just as the oppressive awe settles over you, movement flickers at the edge of vision. But before you can move closer, figures emerge from the shadows above. Two robed humans, their pale gray mantles marked with faint spiral glyphs, descend lightly to block your path. The air around them bends and ripples, like heat shimmering off desert stone — the mark of air magic, tightly leashed and waiting. One raises a hand, palm outward in warning, his voice clipped and emotionless:

A moment later, the scrape of boots against stone draws your eye upward. Tywin Terrorwind steps onto the ledge above, his feathered cloak snapping sharply in the mounting wind. He regards you with narrowed eyes, voice cold and final: "You are not permitted to go further."
He pauses, then adds with almost courteous detachment: "The Commander would not wish you to overextend yourselves. Rest may serve you better than curiosity."
Behind him, the wind seems to still. Not calm — but held. Waiting.
"You will come back."
No more needs to be said. You are not being attacked. But you are no longer welcome here.
"This place is not for you — not yet."

The journey back to Feathergale Spire is quiet. Tywin leads the way — mounted, silent — flanked by the two robed cultists. They never speak, never smile, never look back. You ride behind them. Not bound. Not threatened. But watched. Every step. The canyon winds beneath you like a sleeping serpent. Even the wind seems quieter now.

tr.td: You realize: this is not a friendly escort. This is a controlled return. Every movement is shadowed. Your pace is not your own. You are being treated like prisoners — just without the chains.
You sense tension, but chalk it up to Tywin’s usual severity. You feel watched… but not contained. Yet.

text.p: If a fight ensues then they can fight but reinforcements arrive shortly after and the party is forced to surrender.
If the party does not resist:
text.h: Arrival at the Spire, Stable-Level Approach
text.p: The approach to the Spire is not through the grand gate this time. You’re led along the outer spiral path, wind rising as you ascend toward the carved base of the tower. A low stone archway opens into the Spire’s underground level — the stables, where the wind knights’ hippogriffs are housed. Inside, the air is warm and musky with the scent of straw, oil, and beast. Feathers drift through the beams of torchlight, and stable hands pause to watch you pass. The passage from the stables rises via a curved staircase that leads you into the tower’s core. No fanfare. No trumpet. Just the sound of your boots echoing on stone.

As the spiral stairs rise from the stables into the heart of the tower, the soft murmur of voices fades behind stone. Then, the great doors swing open, revealing the familiar vaulted chamber. Warm light spills from the twin hearths. The long, curved table is set for dinner — polished goblets, fragrant dishes, and carefully arranged place settings. Tapestries sway gently in the upper breeze. Mounted heads on the walls seem to watch in silence.

Thurl Merosska stands at the far end of the room in full regalia, his feathered cloak perfectly arranged. He greets you with a smooth smile and a slight inclination of the head — formal, respectful, measured.

p.i: "Welcome back. The Spire is grateful. You’ve done what few would dare. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed. Rest. Eat. You’ve earned both.”

text.p: He gestures lightly toward the feast.
There is no fanfare, no applause — just a carefully set table and Thurl’s unwavering hospitality.
Optional Insight Check (DC 13): There’s something in the tone — not cold, but deliberate. As though each word was chosen ahead of time.
If the Party Asks:

list.li: “Where are the Wyndwyrds?”

text.p: Thurl answers with a nod and a slight shrug:

p.i: “They completed their engagement and departed earlier this evening. Their performance was appreciated.”

text.p: He moves on before questions can linger.

list.li: “Where are Savra and Eren?”

text.p: “They’re speaking privately. Family matters, I believe.”
His smile doesn’t change. The kind of answer meant to reassure — or to end the question.
text.h: The Pinnacle Betrayal: Sacrifices to Yan-C-Bin
text.p: Sleep comes uneasily within the tower’s stone walls. And then — darkness shatters. You awaken with a jolt, but cannot move. Your body is bound, arms and legs locked in place by invisible force. You can feel cold stone beneath you, and wind biting into your skin. Magic binds you. The air itself grips your limbs — and you are not alone. You're being dragged. Shadows and figures glide around you as you are pulled upward — stair after stair, through cold halls — until finally, your captors reach the top You are thrown down onto the cold, slick stones of the pinnacle platform, the tower’s apex exposed to the midnight storm. The wind howls. Lightning crackles in the black clouds above, and the air itself seems to press downward — angry, waiting. Rain lashes your faces. You squint through the storm and see you are not the only prisoners. The Wyndwyrds are here — stripped of their instruments, on their knees, heads bowed low. Eren is beside them, barely conscious, blood trailing from the corner of his mouth. All of them are bound — just as you are.
Before you stands a row of familiar figures, now cloaked in menace:

list.li: Tywin Terrorwind, eyes glittering with contempt, hand resting on his blade.
Savra Belabranta, standing still beside Thurl — her face blank, gaze distant. There's a strange softness to her eyes — not clarity, but enchantment.
Thurl Merosska, commander no longer — but high priest, eyes burning with purpose.
And at the center, a new figure:

text.p: She is taller than the rest, wrapped in silk-thin robes that swirl in the wind though she stands perfectly still. Feathered wings shimmer behind her, fanning gently with unnatural grace. Her eyes gleam violet beneath a silver circlet, and her voice, when it comes, is no more than a whisper — and yet it carries above the storm:

p.i: “The wind accepts you. You will drift. You will fall. You will rise... as part of something far greater.”

text.p: She smiles like a child playing queen.

p.i: “I am Aerisi Kalinoth — daughter of the skies, prophet of the Eye, princess of the storm. Your offering pleases me.”

text.p: Thurl steps forward, arms raised, voice booming with unnatural weight as he begins the invocation:

p.i: “Yan-C-Bin, Prince of Evil Air, Master of the Infinite Skies — we offer to you the breath of those who have breathed too long!”

text.p: He turns his gaze to you — calm, certain:

p.i: “Your lives will sanctify this tower. And your deaths will carry our devotion to the blackest heights.”

text.p: Thurl turns slightly, voice quiet now.
Tywin steps forward, unsheathing his blade with an audible hiss. He gives the party a sideways glance, his voice filled with cruel satisfaction:

p.i: “You should have stayed in your rooms.”

text.p: He moves to the first Wyndwyrd. Without hesitation, he drives the blade in, and with a flourish, casts the body from the pinnacle. The wind takes it. No sound. No end. He walks to the second. Then the third. Each time, a small smirk. Each time, a theatrical pause.
“Music... so fleeting, isn’t it?”
The final Wyndwyrd slumps. The wind devours them all. Rain drives harder. Lightning dances above you. The Prophet watches silently, as if waiting for the storm to speak back.
As the Last Wyndwyrd Falls…

Tywin withdraws his blade from the final Wyndwyrd. Their body vanishes into the wind like the others, swallowed by the storm. The Prophet Aerisi Kalinoth spreads her wings above the pinnacle, hair whipping in the maelstrom.

p.i: "And now, you. Your lives will lift us higher. The wind demands your breath."

text.p: Thurl steps forward, raising his hands to the sky as the storm surges with elemental energy. But then — something cracks. Not thunder. Not stone. Something deeper.

From one of your pouches, the Book of Grudges begins to tremble — glowing faintly with ancestral dwarven script. The wind around you pushes in — and then is forced back. Chains of air snap. Your limbs lurch free. The invisible binds that held you break apart in flashes of silver-blue light, scattering like ash in a gale. You land on your feet — still wind-bitten, soaked, but free. The wind does not welcome you anymore. You stand against it.

list.li: Aerisi lets out a shriek, rising higher into the storm on phantom wings.

text.p: "NO! They are MINE!"

list.li: Thurl draws his blade in one smooth motion, his ceremonial calm breaking into zealous fury.
Tywin’s grin returns, even broader.

text.p: “Finally.”

list.li: Savra, still under enchantment, steps forward with the others — but her sword-hand trembles.

text.p: Enemies:

list.li: Thurl Merosska (high-ranking paladin/cult zealot)
Tywin Terrorwind (elite air knight, aggressive, sadistic)
Savra Belabranta (enchanted, torn)
Aerisi Kalinoth (hovering above, issuing commands)

text.p: Aerisi does not fight directly yet — she watches, commands, and lets the cult prove itself.

list.li: If the Party Tries to Kill Tywin:

text.p: As the final blow nears, a sudden shriek rips across the sky —
the wind collapses inward around him, a vortex of razor air shattering your strike.
Tywin is lifted into the air by a column of screaming wind, his form vanishing into the clouds above.
A disembodied whisper rumbles across the spire:
“HE IS CLAIMED. HE IS MINE.” — Yan-C-Bin.
Tywin is gone.

list.li: If the Party Defeats Thurl:

text.p: Thurl dies with no glory. His blade falls from his hand, eyes wide with disbelief — not at your strength, but that Aerisi did nothing to stop it.
"I served… the sky…"
He falls. The wind does not catch him.

list.li: If the Party Spares or Breaks Savra:

text.p: A strong persuasion or magical intervention (or if she’s reduced to 0 HP nonlethally) can shake her enchantment. Her sword lowers. Tears streak down her face, barely visible through the storm.
"Eren… what have I done…"
She may turn sides, or flee, depending on the moment.

list.li: If the Party Falls (Defeated):

text.p: As the last of you collapse, wind swirls violently, wrapping around your bodies like a noose. You are lifted — broken, dazed — to the edge of the spire. With a word from Aerisi, you are cast into the storm below. But before the black claims you— Wingbeats. Talons. You are caught in midair — your bodies cradled by feathered arms and wind-scoured wings. The Aarakocra dive from the storm — intercepting you in silence — and vanish into the clouds, carrying your unconscious forms toward safety.
The winds have stopped.
For the first time in days, Feathergale Spire stands still. Its banners hang limp, and the eerie whistling through stone corridors has faded to silence. The tower feels… waiting.
It has been three days since the battle at the pinnacle. The wyndwyrds are gone. Thurl is dead. The ritual is broken - for now.
The last of the Feathergale cultists have been purged from the tower. Their silence echoes through the spire's halls. In their place, life has begun to stir again.
On the third morning, the sound of horns calls from the west.
Eren has returned.

The caravan is modest but disciplined - three supply carts, twelve guards in polished gear, and a Red Larch banner snapping in the breeze. Their boots hit the stone with intent. Supplies are unloaded, shops set up in cleared chambers within the tower's lower halls. The scent of fresh food, firewood, and new leather fills the air.

Savra meets Eren in the great hall. There are no embraces - only nods, and quiet understanding. She has grown sterner since the ritual. Eren seems changed too - weight on his shoulders that wasn't there before.
Outside the tower, the sky remains overcast.
Thunder rumbles somewhere in the distance.
Clouds gather slowly, creeping across the horizon like a tide rolling in.
And the air - the air feels colder with each passing hour.
Scene Setup: War Council / Assignment Phase Ends
The players have made their decisions:

list.li: Assigned guards to defend, scout, or attack
Met the traders and sidekicks
Prepared or resupplied

text.p: The spire is quiet again. Not in peace — in waiting. Thunder still creeps over the hills. The traders have settled into storage halls and open galleries, while the guards take watch on the outer ledges.
Savra approaches the party after they've completed their planning. She looks tired, but composed. The armor fits her now — not like a costume, but a choice.
Savra (quietly):

p.i: “When we first wore these cloaks, I thought it was for honor. For glory. But this place… it doesn’t give you that. It gives you silence. And wind. And the promise that something is always watching.”

text.p: She glances at the sky through an arrow slit.

p.i: “If the cult strikes first, they won’t do it in the open. Not with banners. It’ll be shadows. Whispers. Assassins before armies.”

text.p: She turns back to the group:

p.i: “You’ve bought us time. Use it well. If you want answers... we’ll need to find them before the next wind rises.”

text.p: Later that evening, as the tower dims and torches are lit, an injured Aarakocra scout stumbles into the lower courtyard — bloody, winded, and terrified.

p.i: “The shrikes— caw —they came from the west cliffs. My kin... they’re pinned near the Dead Rocks! Too many winds! Too many blades! Please...”

text.p: Savra or Eren urges the party to intervene. This becomes your first Act 2 side mission: rescuing the Aarakocra, which in turn rewards them with a wind trinket and deeper understanding of the cult's reach.
text.h: Narrative: The Approach to Knifepoint Gully
text.p: The sun beats down harshly as you descend into the valley, the wind whispering erratically across the rocky terrain. Dry shrubs twist in the midday breeze. The air here feels thinner—charged. Ahead, the jagged walls of Knifepoint Gully rise once more, a familiar scar splitting the earth.
But something’s wrong.

You hear it before you see it—a low, resonant hum, unnatural and deep, like a great beast inhaling. The wind rushes forward and then swirls back violently, forming a towering tornado at the mouth of the gully. Dust and debris churn in the air, forming a shrieking, spiraling barrier that touches sky and stone.
The wind doesn’t move. It holds steady—deliberate. Guarded.
Savra narrows her eyes, wind tugging at her cloak.
“The cult’s sealed the gully… They’re preparing for a counterattack.”
The implications hang heavy in the air.

Before you can react further, shadows break across the ridge above you. A piercing shriek cuts through the wind, followed by a war horn blast. Figures emerge from the vortex—Feathergale Knights, robed initiates of the air cult, backed by strange elemental scouts carried on controlled gusts.
Clues That Can Be Dropped

list.li: A map with wind-marked paths showing the rotating shift of cult patrols (for the supply route)
A sigil-etched charm that matches markings on the Howling Plateau (key hint)
A note mentioning: “Prepare the barricade—Wind’s Eye Totem must be aligned before sunset.”
An incomplete prayer scroll referencing a “bypass beneath the roots of stone” (backdoor clue)

text.p: With the last of the cultists fallen, the storm-charged air crackles with lingering energy. Dust swirls low across the canyon floor, mingling with stray feathers and the sharp scent of ozone. In the cultists' belongings, you uncover scraps of parchment and carved fragments of stone—hastily drawn maps, strange glyphs, and one clear phrase:
Nearby, one of the shattered stones bears a spiral motif—eerily similar to those etched into tapestries back at Feathergale Spire.
Prompt a DC 13 History Check

list.li: If a player succeeds:

text.p: As you study the glyphs, the memory stirs—a page from a wind cultic manuscript you skimmed in the Spire’s library. You recognize the phrase ‘Wind’s Eye’ and its link to an elemental convergence described in ancient script. It could be referencing a totem... or a ritual site.

list.li: If no one succeeds:

text.p: Savra narrows her eyes, turning the tablet fragment slowly in her hand.

p.i: “I know this symbol,” she mutters. “It was scribbled in the margins of an old scroll in the Spire’s library. I didn’t think it meant anything. But... it’s all connected, isn’t it?”

text.p: A sudden roar pulls your attention back to the gully.

The tornado barrier surges—thickening, twisting violently in place, now a cyclone of howling wind and stinging debris. It does not fade. It grows. Stone is torn loose from the canyon wall. The very wind screams with warning. Savra takes a step back, shielding her eyes.

p.i: “They’ve sealed the gully. The cult’s preparing for a counterattack. We won’t get through this way now.”

text.p: She glances toward the horizon.

p.i: “But the Spire may hold the rest of the answer. If there's a way past this... it's in those records.”

text.p: Thunder rolls in the distance. The wind cools. Above, the sky darkens.
Payout
reroll stores
text.h: Return to the Spire to Analyze Clues & Plan (Safe Hub Option)
text.p: Reason: Review the sigils, symbols, and maps with Savra or one of the scholars from Red Larch or the traders.
Result: Savra may help identify the Wind’s Eye Totem as a myth related to the Howling Plateau, or recall that older Feathergale scouts mentioned "air shifts" at specific times in that region.
Benefit: Prepares them for their next destination and lets them manage tower defenses.
Path of the Wind Totem (The Key Route)
Codename: The Gale Lock
Description: A hidden shrine deep in the Howling Plateau houses an elemental totem. Activating or destroying it disrupts the tornado barrier long enough to allow entry into Knifepoint Gully.
Advantages: Permanently opens the temple front entrance. A clear, direct victory against the cult’s magical defenses.
Challenges:
Heavy cultist defense, possibly led by a named lieutenant or elemental horror.
Harsh weather hazards (wind bursts, unstable footing).
Possibly guarded by a bound air elemental or cursed knight.
Backdoor Route (The Maze Path)
Codename: The Hollow Spiral
Description: A forgotten cave system beneath the Sighing Valley—narrow, damp, winding corridors once used by dwarves or outcasts to escape.
Advantages:
Least defended route—minimal cultist patrols inside.
Opportunities for stealth, exploration, or puzzle-solving.
Challenges:
Maze-like layout with branching paths.
Lurking cave creatures or abandoned traps.
Risk of cave-ins or getting lost without proper skill checks.
Tight hallways are not ideal to move
Codename: Whispers on the Wind
Description: The cult opens a brief window for supply drops—rare moments when the wind wall weakens. The party can disguise themselves as cultists and slip in with the next caravan.
Advantages:
Straight into the heart of the temple.
Requires minimal combat up front—good for intrigue-heavy parties.
Challenges:
Surrounded by enemies once inside.
Requires perfect timing, acting, and stealth.
If discovered, triggers a difficult infiltration fight against elite forces.

The twisting corridors finally give way to a wider chamber, its air heavy with the scent of extinguished smoke. Scattered bedrolls circle the blackened stones of an old fire pit, cold and long dead. Around the chamber, crates and barrels sit forgotten — cracked lids, empty sacks, nothing of value but the impression of lives once camped here.
The silence is thick, broken only by the drip of water from somewhere deeper in the stone. It feels too still, as though the camp had been abandoned only moments before.

Exhaustion weighs on every step. You’ve pushed hard, and what remains of your strength is little more than stubborn resolve. Though the faint breath of wind promises an exit not far beyond, the body demands rest.
Ask the party to determine their Guard Rotation
Guard rotations are quickly agreed upon, and one by one the party settles into uneasy sleep.

Hours pass in the half-light of torches and fading coals. Then, during one of the watches, the chamber shifts. At first it’s nothing — a flicker in the corner of the eye, the sense of movement in still air. When the watcher looks again, a folded piece of parchment lies on the ground near the cold fire pit, where nothing had been before.

The paper bears a downward-pointing equilateral black triangle with an inverted Y-shape inscribed within it, only the faintest texture like impressions pressed too hard and then erased. An odd weight hangs in the air around it, as if the silence of the cavern is leaning in.

p.i: A test of memory or knowledge stirs:
o recognize what this strange parchment once bore. But even a scholar’s eye will likely falter here.

list.li: Success: The watcher recalls scraps of forbidden lore — that such marks once denoted rituals tied to the Elder Elemental Eye. Even knowing this much sends a chill through them.
Failure: The parchment’s meaning slips away. At most, it feels eerie — a phantom clue too faint to grasp.

text.p: Should the watcher take it, the paper feels ordinary enough in hand. Yet when shown to another, the markings are gone — the parchment nothing more than blank, brittle scrap. Only the one who found it can recall what they thought they saw.
Sleep resumes, but the chamber feels less secure now. The parchment remains in memory, if not in hand, and the cold of the cave presses in a little deeper.
text.h: Scene: Cave Exit — The Wind Bears Two Truths
text.p: The party awakens around 2300, weary but restored — wounds closed, spell slots replenished, though the memory of battle lingers like smoke in the air. The cavern twists upward until the rocky mouth opens to the night. The stars gleam cold above the plateau, and the distant thunder of the storm wall rumbles faintly.
A rush of wings sweeps down from the darkness. Dust stirs as Savra Belabranta and three Aarakocra land just outside the exit. She steps forward, voice firm and breathless with urgency.
text.frame: “I found it—the answer. The barrier at Knifepoint Gully is bound to a Wind Totem. That is how the cult sealed the temple. But this path…” she gestures to the tunnel behind you “…it bypasses the storm ward entirely. You already stand behind their shield.”
text.p: Her expression hardens, the words carrying both triumph and warning.
text.frame: “But know this—if you march now, you march alone. No one from the Spire can follow you through the storm. The Ember Lances cannot aid your assault.”
text.p: Savra takes a moment to look over the group. Relief touches her face—then fades. Her eyes flicker again, counting. Her voice falters.
text.frame: “…Where is Rella?”
text.p: Roleplay Required — the party must explain or conceal what happened.
Her shoulders stiffen, grief flooding her features. For a breath she is silent, jaw clenched, until sorrow forces its way into words.
text.frame: “No… the Ember Lances will be devastated. She was one of our finest.”
text.p: Savra kneels, touching the ground with one hand, bowing her head. When she rises, her voice is steady, though heavy.
text.frame: “Please. Allow the Aarakocra to return her to the Spire. She deserves her rites, her memory honored in the place she swore to protect.”
text.p: If the party agrees immediately:

list.li: Savra bows her head in gratitude.
The Aarakocra step forward reverently to lift Rella’s body.

text.p: If the party hesitates (Persuasion DC 14):

list.li: On success: Savra’s grief softens.
On failure: she insists, though her trust in the party cools.

text.p: Closing Beat
The Aarakocra take flight with Rella’s body, wings vanishing into the dark. Savra remains, planting her spear into the dirt.
text.frame: “Then it is decided. The Temple of Howling Hatred stands before us, and I will march with you. Whatever storm awaits—we will tear it down.”
text.p: The winds stir the plateau, carrying both the weight of Rella’s loss and the promise of the battle ahead.
The night air cuts sharp as the party advances from the cavern. The path widens into an intersection of stone and scrub, the ground still humming faintly with the storm’s unseen power.
Ahead, the sound of horns, wings, and marching boots grows. Cresting a rise, the party witnesses a force moving like a storm front:
Dozens of Air Cultists in ceremonial mail, their banners whipping.
A squadron of kenku, voices squawking mimicry as they march in eerie rhythm.
Feathergale Knights mounted on hippogriffs, silver helms gleaming in the moonlight.
And towering over all — a wyvern, leathery wings snapping as it takes to the air, driven forward by handlers.
The column is heading away from the temple, flying and marching toward Knifepoint Gully.
If the party says nothing / hesitates:

list.li: Savra narrows her eyes, tone grim:

text.frame: “That is no patrol. They mean to strike Feathergale Spire. If they fall, the plateau belongs to the cult.”
text.p: If the party voices intent to turn back:

list.li: Savra raises her hand, shaking her head firmly:

text.frame: “No. The Spire must hold its own. If we abandon this chance, the cult’s storm will never break. Our task lies here.”

p.b: Decision Point — The Plan of Attack

text.p: Savra turns to the party leader, her voice carrying over the winds.
text.frame: “The choice is yours. What is our plan for the Temple?”

list.li: If the party suggests a direct assault:

text.p: Savra warns:
text.frame: “Bravery will see us slain. We cannot face their whole strength head-on without the Lances at our back.”

list.li: If the party falters or cannot decide:

text.p: Savra suggests:
text.frame: “Then we move with subtlety. The plateau forces are away, and their eyes will be on the Spire. Now is the time to slip the blade between their ribs.”
text.p: Insight (DC 14): A player realizes the force’s departure thins the defenses at the temple entrance.
History (DC 12): A player recalls the Spire has weathered sieges before — they are built to hold against such assaults, reinforcing Savra’s point.
Persuasion (DC 15, party leader only): If they insist on diverting to aid the Spire, Savra reluctantly agrees but warns the cult may reinforce the Temple while they are gone.

The wind shifts, carrying the banners of the departing army like phantoms into the night. Behind lies the battered road back to Feathergale Spire. Ahead lies the shadowed maw of the Temple of Howling Hatred, its storm barrier looming like a living wall.
The crossroads waits — and with it, the weight of choice.

linklist.link: Story: Episode#2.50.01 Temple of Howling Hatred Entrance

id-00051.name: Episode#2.50.01 Temple of Howling Hatred Entrance

text.frame: "The carved reliefs of two dwarves face one another in profile to complete an arch beyond the ledge. Through the arch, the blocky contours of a lost dwarven city sprawl in the subterranean night. From somewhere within comes an agonized wail, followed by a breathless ramble of whimpering pleas. Then the whole city seems to join the chorus with the screams of creatures mad from torment."
text.p: As the party approaches the entrance, Savra slows, eyes narrowing on the carved dwarven reliefs.
text.frame: “These faces… I’ve seen them. But not like this. It’s as if they watched us — every time we entered.” She places her hand lightly against the stone arch — reverent, but wary. “There were rituals here. I remember the chanting, the way our footsteps echoed through the halls. I wasn’t myself. None of us were.” A beat passes. Then, as the wails echo, she flinches — not from fear, but recognition. “That sound... it's not real. They play it like music. The cult calls it ‘The Chorus of Clarity.’ They believe pain sharpens the soul.” She doesn’t elaborate further — her fists are clenched now, jaw tight.

tr.td: You notice a faint carving on the base of one dwarven statue — a downward-pointing triangle with an inverted Y. Same as the vanishing parchment symbol. Only visible to the one who found it.
These dwarven structures are authentic but defiled — re-carved with subtle cult sigils. The layout once held ceremonial meaning, now twisted.
Savra is hiding fear — this place disturbs her deeply, but she’s trying to stay composed. Something here feels familiar.
The wails are not natural. They’re ritualized, part of an air cult practice known as The Chorus of Clarity — meant to strip ego and “open the soul.”

text.p: Savra’s Memory Checks (DM rolls privately)

tr.td: “I remember chants echoing through here… not words, but rhythm. It made us move in time, like puppets.”
“This corridor was used for processions. But the statues weren’t always here — they were dragged from elsewhere, meant to ‘watch’ us.”
Savra stiffens. “That mark… I saw it once. Not here. Not awake. In a dream. A warning, I think…”

linklist.link: Story: Episode#2.50.01 Temple of Howling Hatred Entrance

text.frame: "A squat stone gatehouse stands at the entrance to the dwarven city. Beyond the open gates, an arched corridor zigzags past sturdy stone walls where arrow slits squint from every angle. At the far end of this murderous hallway stands the entrance to this lost dwarven city."

p.b: As the party pauses at the entrance:

text.p: Savra’s eyes flash wide as she studies the corridor.
“This is a dwarven kill hall. We used it… no, they used it — to herd invaders into slaughter. The slits are everywhere. This isn’t a battle. It’s a bloodletting.”
“Don’t stop. Move. They’ll break us if we stall.”
If the party suggests standing and fighting, she growls:
“You’ll feed the stones with your blood — just like the last ones.”

tr.td: You spot the arrow slits and note how they’re positioned to allow crossfire from multiple angles. (Dwarves have Advantage.)
You realize the tormenting cries are not real — mimicry. Some voices may even resemble fallen allies.
You quickly piece together that staying in the killbox is suicidal — fighting here without cover gives the enemy a massive advantage.
Attempt to dash through the corridor quietly or low to the ground. Success: Disadvantage on one kenku volley.
If a player declares a full-speed dash from one end to the other, consider awarding half damage or Disadvantage on attacks from kenku this round.
Ideal outcome. Possibly take a few arrows, but avoid prolonged combat.
Kenku rotate between slits, close shutters, and use hit-and-hide tactics. Encourage disengagement.
If hit, she may stagger and yell: “Go! I said GO!” Reinforces urgency.
They retreat toward A12 silently. You can seed a named kenku there for later.

linklist.link: Story: Episode#2.50.04 Plaza of the Muses
Story: Episode#2.50.01 Temple of Howling Hatred Entrance

text.h: A4. Plaza of the Muses (With Savra Present)
text.frame: A stone fountain stands in the middle of a grand plaza, its sides sculpted into the shapes of dwarves bearing drums and horns. Around it, several figures in feathered garb blow a shrill, discordant tune on flutes made of bone. The music grates against the ear — uneven, desperate, like a song no one wants to hear repeated. One figure stands apart. A lean elf with eyes like silver smoke watches the others with open disdain, his own flute still held at his side.
text.p: If the players investigate the scene before combat or audition:

list.li: The feathered robes worn by the initiates appear identical to those worn by the Windwyrds executed at Feathergale Spire — tattered but recognizable.
Bone Flutes appear to be carved from humanoid remains.
Confirms: the flutes are made from the bones of humanoids — polished and hollowed for windflow. Likely from former cultists who failed.
One flute has initials burned into the bone, matching one of the names the party saw on execution rolls at the Spire — or even a bard the players met briefly.
Windharrow immediately stops playing and snarls at the initiates.

text.frame: “They bleat like goats! Tell me you’ve come to rescue me from this insult to air and art.”

list.li: He then notices Savra — his eyes pass over her with mild curiosity, then dismiss her entirely.

text.frame: “And who’s this? Another hopeful whisper in Aerisi’s storm? No — don’t tell me. Let your breath prove you.”
text.p: Upon entering the plaza, Savra stiffens the moment she hears the music. Her grip tightens on her weapon, but she doesn’t act.

p.b: When Windharrow dismisses her, she speaks under her breath:

text.frame: “I stood guard while these songs were played… I thought it was art then. I thought I was protecting beauty. It was just noise. Just bones.”
text.p: If any player hesitates about performing or parleying:
text.frame: “It’s your choice. But that man is poison — even when he smiles.”
text.p: She remains close, watching Windharrow and the initiates like a hawk. If a performance goes poorly or Windharrow begins to insult the party, Savra visibly tenses, ready to intervene if needed.

p.b: On success (Performance check DC 12 or creative flair), he:

list.li: Gives them robes and flutes.
Says they will “travel deeper into the Temple soon to meet Aerisi herself.”
Warns: “Do not play unless instructed. And do not displease her — she prefers her flutes…hollow.”
Windharrow casts Mirror Image on Round 1.
Uses Cutting Words as a reaction.
If reduced to half HP or lower, he flees toward Area A19.
The initiates fight poorly, willing to die to protect him if commanded.

text.p: If combat erupts:

list.li: Savra immediately joins the fight, targeting Windharrow.
If Windharrow mocks her during the battle:

text.frame: “Oh, so you do remember me.”
“Only as a failure. Let's keep that streak alive.”

list.li: If Windharrow flees, Savra shouts after him:

text.frame: “Keep running, coward. When next we meet, you’ll answer for everything.”

p.b: If the party takes the robes and instruments:

list.li: They gain advantage on Deception checks when interacting with Air Cultists while disguised.
Group Stealth checks to infiltrate deeper areas can use the robes as a rationale for reduced suspicion.
Insight DC 13 by cultists may still reveal minor flaws in behavior if the party hesitates or acts off-script.

linklist.link: Encounter: Episode#2.50.04 Plaza of the Muses

text.frame: A deep moat surrounds a grand stone plaza centered on a two-tiered step pyramid. Broad stone colonnades to the north and east span the water, supported by massive dwarf statues submerged to the neck. A short bridge lies to the south. The rushing water flows west into a chasm, the roar of the waterfall thundering through the vault. High above, perched atop the pyramid like a predator on its roost, is a cloaked figure astride a wyvern — Kaz Hanar, Skyweaver of the Air Cult. Mineral flecks sparkle in the ceiling like a starry sky, but all eyes are drawn to the beating wings and narrowed gaze descending from above.
text.p: As the party approaches, Kaz Hanar swoops down on his wyvern, landing with a tremor on the stone colonnade. Windharrow steps forward with performative calm.
Kaz Hanar (suspicious):
text.frame: “Windharrow. You bring more flutists? What is this — an orchestra?”
text.p: Windharrow (annoyed but cautious):
text.frame: “They’re mine. A new ensemble. I’ve prepared them to play for the Prophet.”
text.p: Kaz (snorts):
text.frame: “For Aerisi? Then let me hear them first.”
text.p: Windharrow (defensive):
text.frame: “They’ve already played. You’re not the audience that matters.”
text.p: Kaz (grinning, taunting):
text.frame: “You don’t command me, songbird. If they want passage, they’ll play. Or they’ll fall.”

list.li: One assigned lead must roll Performance DC 13.
The rest of the party must each make Performance checks (DC 10 suggested).
At least 50% of the party must succeed or Kaz refuses passage.

text.p: Kaz listens in eerie silence. The wyvern clicks its claws across the stone as the final note fades.
Kaz leans back with a satisfied smirk:
text.frame: “You’re better than the last batch. They choked — quite literally. Go on. The Prophet awaits.”
text.p: He waves them toward A18 and takes flight, circling above.
Kaz snarls:
text.frame: “Pathetic. Noise. You think Aerisi wants this filth in her ears?”
text.p: He commands his wyvern to block the path. Unless placated or tricked, combat is imminent.

tr.td: Kaz might accept treasure, a relic, or a favor
With clever RP, Kaz can be convinced Aerisi requested them personally
On Insight DC 14, Kaz sees through him — growing distrustful or mocking

text.p: Kaz swoops in aggressively, circling with his wyvern before landing hard and glaring at the group.
His eyes lock onto Savra immediately.
text.frame: “Well, well… the traitor returns. What happened, Savra? Miss the feel of the ropes at Obelisk Row? I’ll tell Aerisi her favorite toy came crawling back. I’m sure she’ll love to see what tricks you remember.”
text.p: Wisdom Saving Throw DC 14 (DM roll):
Success: She tightens her grip, eyes burning with shame and fury.
text.frame: “Say one more word and you’ll be picking teeth out of your wyvern’s dung.”
text.p: Failure: She freezes, stunned and silent — visibly shaking, breathing unevenly. (Charisma-based characters may try to help her recover mid-scene.)
Unless the party immediately withdraws or surrenders, Kaz attacks. He's expecting weakness — and wants to demonstrate dominance. This is not a parley.
If combat breaks out, run Kaz + wyvern encounter as written (see PotA Ch. 7 – Skyweaver statblock).

linklist.link: Story: Episode#2.50.04 Plaza of the Muses

text.frame: Three tapered obelisks, their sides inscribed with ancient pictographs, stand in a row, their peaks scraping the fifteen-foot-high ceiling. Each obelisk has a gaunt human tied to its base. Around the obelisks, a colored cobblestone mosaic depicts Moradin, a huge warhammer slung over his shoulder. Lashed to the obelisks with thick ropes are three Howling Hatred initiates, suffering from extreme starvation. They are emaciated, barely conscious, with terrible welts along their skeletal frames.
text.p: If characters try to free them, they protest, claiming they are learning to "survive on air alone."
text.h: If the Party is in Disguise (with Windharrow)
text.p: Windharrow leads the party through the chamber like a priest at a gallery opening. His voice rings with mock reverence:
Windharrow’s Dialogue:
text.frame: “Behold… Obelisk Row. The Song of Emptiness begins here.” (He gestures with a theatrical sweep toward the bound cultists.) “These are aspirants of silence. They fast until the burden of flesh lightens, until only breath and will remain. It is… a sacred trial. Part devotion, part penance. You’ll learn the rhythms eventually.” (He smirks at a barely conscious initiate.) “They do this willingly. They believe, as we all must, that to please the Prophet is to please the wind. Now hush. We do not disturb those who are learning to fly.”
text.p: He doesn't stop to engage unless questioned — this is a performance for him, not a conversation.
Insight DC 12: Windharrow doesn’t fully believe in this ritual — his tone betrays a degree of sarcasm or theatricality. He’s playing the part to impress the Prophet (or out of fear).
Medicine DC 10: These people are on the verge of death. A few hours or a stiff breeze could kill them.

Performance/Religion RP Option: A character who respectfully mimics cult behavior (bowing, offering praise to the wind) may earn Windharrow’s nod of approval. No mechanical effect, but it preserves the disguise.
Savra says nothing.
She follows silently, but her posture becomes increasingly rigid. A sharp observer may catch her hand tremble slightly or see her avert her gaze from the bound cultists.
If a party member tries to check on her:
Insight DC 13: She’s emotionally shaken — holding back visible pain or memory.
She keeps silent so as not to risk the disguise — but this moment stays with her.
text.h: If the Party is Not in Disguise
text.p: As the party steps into the chamber, Savra freezes in the entryway.
text.frame: “This is how they prove themselves. They call it devotion — surviving on air alone. But it’s not faith. It’s... indoctrination.”
text.p: Wisdom Saving Throw DC 13:
Success: Savra grits her teeth and holds her ground. She speaks:
text.frame: “They tried to put me here once. I was spared — someone else took my place. Don’t think for a moment I deserved that mercy.”
text.p: Failure: She stumbles back, knees weak. Her eyes are distant, haunted.
text.frame: “No—no, not again— I was here. I was here. I can still feel the ropes—!”

list.li: She is overwhelmed by the memory, loses her composure, and cannot speak further for 1–2 minutes unless consoled.

text.p: A PC using Persuasion or Calm Emotions (or physical comfort) may help her recover.
Want to deepen the connection to the vanishing parchment symbol?

p.b: Each obelisk bears a faint carving at the peak, mostly worn smooth:
