list.li: DC 15 Perception or DC 12 Religion identifies it as the downward triangle with inverted Y — symbol of the Elder Elemental Eye.
One cultist murmurs “The Eye sees only the empty.”

text.p: This connects the earlier parchment with real-world cult rituals — and can escalate mystery/horror for the party member who saw the symbol before.

linklist.link: Story: Episode#2.50.04 Plaza of the Muses

text.h: A18. Grand Hall — The Hymn to Yan-C-Bin
text.frame: Two rows of solemn dwarf-carved pillars hold aloft the marble ceiling of this great hall, each statue clutching a stone axe and watching in silence. The ceiling stretches twenty feet above, and twin staircases spiral upward to the east, rail-less and white. In the center of the room, a wind-whipped pit pulses with swirling currents of air. Around it, several cultists in gray feathered robes float a few feet above the ground, arms extended, eyes closed, their voices threading together in a discordant chant. The sound is harsh and reverent — a hymn not made for mortal ears.
text.h: If the Party Enters with Windharrow (Still in Disguise)
text.p: Windharrow raises his hands as the group enters. The cultists continue their chant, but the guards watch with wary interest.
Windharrow turns to the party:
text.frame: “Behold the hymn of the Prophet. This is the Grand Hall, where voices rise in devotion to the Lord of Rushing Skies — Yan-C-Bin, Prince of Evil Air. They say he is coming — not as a whisper, but as a storm. And when he arrives, this land will be swept clean. The ignorant will drown in dust, and the faithful will soar on winds of purity. He walks toward the pit, gesturing over it as if performing a sermon. And now — we honor him. One final time before the Prophet grants you audience. Play your part in the hymn. Let your breath join the wind.”
“Yan-C-Bin is the Breath That Slays. The Unseen Storm. His presence erodes mountains and hushes suns. But we — we are his song.”
text.p: Windharrow's version paints destruction as transcendence, twisting devotion into a musical metaphor for annihilation. Ritual
Performance DC 15 (by a designated lead, or as group performance — your choice).
Windharrow nods approvingly if the party plays in time and harmony.
text.frame: “Exquisite. You exceed my expectations. When Aerisi hears you, she will know the wind has chosen wisely.”
text.p: He nods toward the staircases leading up to Area A19, allowing them passage.
Windharrow’s face sours, and he raises a hand to halt the chant.
text.frame: “Again. You will not go before the Prophet as discordant wind.”
text.p: Give the party a chance to recover or explain, or risk drawing suspicion from the surrounding guards.
text.h: If the Party is in Disguise but Without Windharrow
text.p: As they enter, the chanting cultists glance over — but the guards hover forward, suspicious.
A hurricane and skyweaver drift closer, eyes narrowed.
text.frame: “Your breath is unfamiliar. What brings you here?”

list.li: Deception, Persuasion, or Performance DC 12 (one character, with help possible).
A plausible explanation (e.g., "sent by Windharrow," "new initiates for the ritual") works.

text.frame: “Very well. Join the chant or stand back. The Prince listens.”
text.p: The party is allowed to remain and may ascend toward A19 if unchallenged further.
text.frame: “This place is not for your breath. Leave — before the wind decides to cast you out.”
text.p: If the party lingers, the guards become hostile.
As soon as they cross into the hall, the guards react.
The hurricane cultist’s voice rises above the chant:
text.frame: “Intruders! Silence them before they defile the hymn!”
text.p: Combat begins.

list.li: All cultists attack as per PotA stat blocks.
Sounds of combat alert A19, but no reinforcements arrive.
The central pit is a shaft leading downward into the Howling Caves (see PotA Ch. 5).
The rising air acts as a feather fall effect.
Trained cultists use cloaks and wingwear to ascend via controlled gliding.

text.frame: The stairs rise to a vast chamber carved in pale marble. A map of an ancient dwarven kingdom is etched into the floor, partially obscured by soot, wine stains, and errant feathers. Towering dwarf statues hold the vaulted ceiling aloft, their once-proud visages draped in gossamer sky-blue curtains. Behind the throne, a spiraling ceremonial horn gleams from its alcove. Atop the dais, the air prophet Aerisi Kalinoth reclines on her throne — a vision of false majesty, her illusory feathered wings fanning the air lazily. Sweet incense wafts in waves around her. Two eerie, wind-born beings — half-seen silhouettes of whirling pressure and whispers — float beside her. One of them has its tendrils curled around a bloodied, restrained Feathergale Knight, who trembles and twitches in pain as the stalker toys with him. Aerisi looks on with dull disinterest, chin resting on her hand.

tr.td: Aerisi questions the party directly → DC 13 Deception/Persuasion to stay
Windharrow present but not with party

text.h: Scene: If Windharrow is Present (With Party)
text.p: Aerisi waves off the tortured knight’s whimpering.
text.frame: “Boring. He thought screaming louder would make the pain meaningful.” (Turning her head lazily) “Perfection, you see, is what I demand… no — what Yan-C-Bin demands.”
text.p: She notices Windharrow and the party.
text.frame: “Windharrow. You bring me… music? Or another disappointment?”
text.p: Windharrow bows low.
text.frame: “Performers, my Prophet. They bring breath worthy of your storm.”
text.p: Aerisi flicks her hand. The Whisper Stalker executes the knight with a quick, horrific twist — then tosses the body aside.
text.frame: “Very well. Let the wind speak through them.”

list.li: One designated lead makes a DC 17 Performance check.
Other party members may attempt DC 13 checks as support (optional — helps roleplay).
If the leader fails, consequences trigger below.
Aerisi leans back, pleased.

text.frame: “You’ve done well. Perhaps not worthless after all.” “Stay. You’ll play again when I claim the Eye. A worthy anthem to our ascension.”
text.h: Aerisi Kalinoth’s Monologue — “The Wind Will Crown Me”
text.frame: (Aerisi rises from her throne. Her illusory wings stretch out as though catching some invisible current. Her voice begins soft, almost reverent, but builds with each breath into manic exaltation.) “Do you feel it? The breath between heartbeats? The hush before a storm tears the sky open?” (She steps down from the dais, pacing with dancer’s grace, arms slowly outstretched.) “It whispers to me — not words, no, but something purer. A current older than flame. Older than stone. Air. Untouched. Unchained. Unforgiving.” (She walks the map of Besilmer etched on the floor, heels clicking softly on ancient lines of kings long dead.) “The others — Gar, Vanifer, Marlos — they still scrape and claw in the dirt like animals, building temples to their petty hungers. But I... I am above them. I see what they cannot.” (She twirls once, sky-blue curtains flaring like wings, her eyes wide and distant.) “The Eye does not weep. The Eye does not burn. The Eye sees.” (Pauses — looking each party member in the eye.) “And soon, it will open for me.” (She walks toward the spiraled horn alcove but turns sharply to face her throne again.) “Feathergale Spire was only the beginning. A feather on the wind. Soon, the wind becomes a gale, and the gale will become a storm — a storm that will sweep away the weak, the faithless, the still-breathing rot of this dying world.” (She raises her arms, voice ringing out across the hall.) “I will take their weapons. The trinkets the other fools guard so jealously. They will bend the knee or be broken. Yan-C-Bin shall rise — and through me, the world shall be scoured clean!” (She lowers her hands slowly, voice soft again.) “And you... you may yet be part of this new world. Or perhaps… just the wind’s next plaything.”
text.p: This monologue is a cue for surprise attack — the party may choose to act at any time.
As the performance sours, Aerisi’s eyes narrow. Her voice cuts like glass.
text.frame: “No... not you.” (She raises Windvane, pointing it at Savra.) “You should know better than anyone what pleases me.”
text.h: Aerisi Kalinoth’s Monologue — “My Feather, My Song”

list.li: Aerisi uses Windvane to cast Dominate Person (DC per spell).
If successful, Savra lowers her weapon, dazed, and steps forward.

text.frame: (Aerisi rises from the throne slowly, wings flaring in spectral shimmer. Her eyes are locked not on the party, but on Savra, who stands paralyzed — trembling — the enchantment in her veins like ice.) “Ah… there she is.” (She smiles, all teeth and cruelty.) “I wondered if I’d broken you so completely that your bones turned to air.” (A step closer. Voice velvet-wrapped in poison.) “But no. My sweet little sparrow returns to the perch.” (She turns slowly, addressing the room, as though introducing a cherished painting.) “Once, she wept in this chamber. So beautiful. So fragile. So obedient.” (She inhales deeply.) “She learned to sing for me. She bled for me. She knelt… for me.” (Eyes flashing to Savra, voice dropping to a whisper.) “Tell them, little feather. Did I not teach you how to fly?” (Savra flinches — a single tear slips down her cheek.) (Aerisi whirls now, voice rising in rapture — speaking to the whole chamber as if before a congregation.) “You see, my flock, there is no room for shame in devotion. No sin in sacrifice. The flesh is weak — but the will can be broken and rebuilt into something… divine.” (She gestures to the pit in A18.) “From these halls, I shall rise. Not as queen. Not as priestess. But as prophet. Herald of Yan-C-Bin. Voice of the Eye.” (Her voice becomes thunder now, carried by gusts that swirl through the chamber’s incense-choked air.) “The Earth wallows. The Flame rages. The Sea drowns in its own sorrow. But air… air lifts. Air whispers. Air judges.” (She spreads her arms wide — illusory wings unfurling, casting long shadows.) “I will retake the Spire. I will gather the weapons. I will open the Eye.” (Then, suddenly quiet again — her gaze returns to Savra.) “And when the world is ash and dust and echoes, I will still remember the sound of your breath against my palm.” (Aerisi slowly returns to her throne and sits, reclined, bored, a queen awaiting her next amusement.) “Now. Entertain me.”
text.p: If any party member tries to break the charm, allow Contested Insight vs Deception or a saving throw reroll with inspiration, love, or heroism.
Aerisi, realizing the party is watching, smirks and summons a gust of wind:
text.frame: “You came to fight? Then breathe your last.”

tr.td: Windharrow is present but not with the party

text.frame: “You let them in? Without my leave?”

tr.td: Party is in disguise without Windharrow

text.frame: “You. Who are you?”

list.li: DC 13 Deception or Performance to convince her they were sent by Windharrow or the Skyweavers.

text.p: Aerisi says
text.frame: “I don’t recall summoning you.”

list.li: Summons a gust of wind to push them back
Whisper Stalkers rush the party.

text.p: Aerisi blows the horn if overwhelmed.

Vessa Marrowind
Trader 2. Stonefall Steel
Durnan Stonefall
Trader 3. The Copper Cache
Rinna Copperhill
The Ember Lance
Guard Composition
Total: 12 guards
8 Red Larch Special Forces:

list.li: 1 Scout
1 Mage (Apprentice Wizard)
3 Fighters
3 Rangers

text.p: Guard Assignments
Each day, guards may be assigned to one of the following roles:

tr.td: Improves spire defense strength. Needed to protect Eren/traders from ambushes.
Reveals clues (1–3 guards must be sent). Risky. Can uncover paths to key, backdoor, or supply window.
Hit cult positions. Slows cult retaliation timer, but reduces spire defense.

text.p: Trigger:

list.li: Used if the party is away from the Spire when the 3-day timer expires.
The cult launches an assault from the air with Hurricanes + knights.

text.p: Step 1: Base Defense Rating
Start with +0 base modifier
Add modifiers:

list.li: +1 per guard left behind (max +12)
+1 if Savra helps coordinate defense
+1 if the Spire has been fortified or prepared (player action)

text.p: Subtract modifiers:

list.li: −2 if fewer than 7 guards are left
−1 if scouts were sent that day and haven’t returned
−1 to −3 if the cult knows they’re under threat (e.g., mini-boss was defeated)

text.p: Step 2: Roll the Defense Check
Roll 1d20 + Defense Mod

list.li: 25+: Flawless defense. No casualties. They even capture one enemy.
20–24: Minor wounds, no deaths.
15–19: One trader or noncombatant injured. Light damage.
10–14: 1 guard is killed, 1 injured. A trader may flee.
5–9: 2 guards killed, 1 trader killed or captured.
<5: Severe losses — 3 guards die, Eren or Savra is gravely wounded or taken.

text.p: Casualty Check (Optional Flare)
Roll 1d4 per casualty to determine who:

list.li: Regular guard
Special classed ally (fighter, mage, etc.)
Named NPC (Eren, Savra, trader)
Random recruitable NPC (if introduced)

text.h: Party A — Post-Kalinoth Session Outline (2.5–4 hrs)

list.li: Let players exhale after the boss fight: resolve loot, questions, and consequences.
Establish Savra (ally) and Eren (your lieutenant NPC—slot in your version) as custodians of Feathergale Spire.
Give the Ember Lances a moment for Rella’s memorial and a branching choice (return to Red Larch for a replacement vs. stay with Savra’s new Stormwing Wardens).
Provide a final trade/level-up window, then launch travel to Red Larch on hippogriffs (slow flyers).
Savra Belabranta: Claims the spire, proposes founding the New Stormwing Wardens to patrol the valley and escort caravans.
Eren: Co-commander or field captain for Savra; can lead riders, escort traders, or accompany the PCs (your call—see Act II choices).
Ember Lances: Mourning Rella; torn between duty to Red Larch and a righteous sky-patrol mission.
Guards & Traders: Hold position briefly to barter, then intend to return to Red Larch in a small convoy.

text.h: Scene I — Aftermath at Feathergale Spire
text.p: Read-Aloud
text.frame: Wind rattles through shattered arrow slits, carrying the smell of spent ozone. Feathergale’s white stone bears fresh scars: spidering cracks across the gate arch, a scorched banner tangled on its pole, shingles shorn from the eaves. Yet the spire stands—guards tightening straps, riders calming restless hippogriffs on the lower perch. Helmets come off, breath fogs in the cooling air, and the first quiet settles after the storm. No one’s fallen.

list.li: Condition: Spire damaged but sound—gates and inner stairs are safe, a few parapet merlons cracked, one loft door splintered.
Casualties: None among your allied defenders. Minor injuries only (treated on site).
Allies on site: Savra Belabranta coordinating repairs; Eren managing the perimeter and prisoners; guards and traders consolidating gear for a later return to Red Larch.
Mounts: Party’s hippogriffs are secured and skittish but fly-worthy (slow flyers).

text.p: 1) Aerisi Kalinoth’s Spellbook (holder automatically notices)
A sheaf of loose notes is tucked among spells—creased and water-spotted.
Names of the other prophets with vague element notes (no statable intel):

list.li: “Mar—earth, stone claims the river.”
“Va—fire, ash to scour the fields.”
“Ga—water, the patient drown.”

text.p: The Elder Eye sigil is sketched repeatedly in the margins. A downward-pointing equilateral black triangle with an inverted Y-shape inscribed within it,
A brief line about the missing delegates: “assets relocated; bargaining intact; elsewhere for now.” No location given.

list.li: Arcana DC 13: Confirms the notes aren’t ritual formula—more like coordination memos; suggests separate strongholds per element.
Religion or History DC 12: Identifies the Elder Eye as a unifying doomsday symbol whispered across cults; not exclusive to Air.
Investigation DC 14: Finds date glyphs implying staggered operations; air actions were meant to soften the region before earth and fire escalations.

text.p: Handout vibe: a single page with names fragmented, an Elder Eye doodle, and one ominous line about “assets relocated.”
2) The Prisoner — Air Cult Hurricane (bound, 1 HP, rattled)
Eren has the Hurricane disarmed near the gate under guard.
What they’ll say freely:

list.li: Knows nothing useful about other prophets beyond element codenames.
Hisses that “our champion will return” to avenge the Air Cult’s fall (speaks with fanatical certainty).
Reveals the champion’s title, not a name (use what fits your canon—e.g., “the Skywrath” / “the Tempest Knight”).
Claims the champion was not present at the Spire fight and answers to no one now that Aerisi has fallen.

text.p: Insight DC 12: The fanaticism is real; they believe the champion lives and is already hunting symbols of victory (banners, names, memorials).

list.li: Deception DC 12 to notice they truly don’t know. They parrot: “Relocated. Useful. Elsewhere.”
Transfer to Savra for judgment,
Bind and march back to Red Larch for questioning, or
Release as a message (earns you a looming vendetta scene later).

text.h: Scene II — Final Trades & Level-Up Window (20–35 min)
text.frame: The great hall has turned into a makeshift bazaar. Quartermasters spread oilcloth over trestles, healers lay out bandages and tinctures, and a scribe scratches names into a ledger while a rack of battered saddles airs by the hearth. Hippogriff feathers drift underfoot like ash.
text.p: Trader 1. Scroll & Serum
Vessa Marrowind
Trader 2. Stonefall Steel
Durnan Stonefall
Trader 3. The Copper Cache
Rinna Copperhill
text.h: Scene III — Rella Sunspur’s Memorial (15–25 min)
text.p: Tone: Earnest, brief, martial. After the market, an Ember Lance sergeant approaches the party and quietly invites them to the parapet. Torches are being set. A small banner with a stitched sunburst is lashed to a cracked merlon.
text.frame: On the wind-washed parapet, helms come off. A simple banner, stitched with a sunburst, lifts in the evening air. Names are spoken; Rella’s most recent deed told plain and proud. A final salute—steel to heart, then skyward.
text.p: 1. Roll Call & Moment of Silence

list.li: The sergeant calls the Lances present; the final name is Rella Sunspur. Heads bow; the wind answers.

text.p: 2. Eulogies (player spotlight)

list.li: Invite one PC to speak a few lines (prompt them—see “Memory Prompts” below).
An Ember Lance follows with a terse, martial eulogy: “She ran first into danger and last from it. The light she carried is not spent.”

text.p: 3.Honors & Token

list.li: A Lance steps forward with a cloth-wrapped pin: the Sunspur Token—a brass sunburst backed by felt.
They present it to the group (or to the PC who speaks), with: “For those who keep others standing.”

text.p: 4. Dedication

list.li: A waterskin is poured out over the stones (or a single torch is snuffed with two fingers). The banner flaps once, then settles.

text.p: 5. Branch (their next step)

list.li: The Lances state their intent and ask for the party’s blessing:

text.p: A) Return to Red Larch to recruit a replacement and report.
B) Pledge to Savra and remain one tenday as auxiliaries to the Stormwing Wardens before rotating home.
text.h: Scene IV — Provisional Garrison & Send-Off(25–40 min)
text.frame: The council room hums with tired purpose. Maps are re-pinned, a cracked banner is tied off with rawhide, and lists are scratched into a soot-smudged ledger. Savra and Eren confer over duty rosters; Ember Lances strip armor and re-wrap grips. A sealed letter waits on the table, the wax still warm.
text.p: Scene Frame: Upper hall / council chamber with maps, torn banners, and scorched stone.

list.li: Command: Savra is Acting Commander of Feathergale Spire until Red Larch confirms. Eren oversees perimeter, drills, and rebuild.
Forces on hand: A skeleton watch (guards + Ember Lances rotating); enough to hold, not patrol.
Traders: Ready to depart within the hour; they’ll go with or without the party’s escort.

text.p: Savra slides over a sealed letter and duplicate copy.

list.li: Subject: “Feathergale Spire secured; request for recruits & supplies.”
Points:

text.p: 1. Spire held after air-cult engagement; no friendly losses. 2. Request 6–10 reliable hands (watchmen, outriders, climbers) and basic stores (rations, saddlery repairs, lamp oil, rope, nails).

3. Recognize Savra Belabranta as Acting Commander pending town approval. 4. Interim charter intent: defend the Spire, support lawful travel, report to Red Larch. 5. Note of captured air-cult hurricane (status: held for questioning; will transfer upon request).
If you want exact text, say the word—I’ll hand you a paste-ready letter block.worker’s Tools DC 12–14: Improvised repairs worth 50–100 gp gear value to the Spire.
Let each PC do one of these; keep to 10–12 minutes total.

list.li: Logistics Push — Persuasion DC 13 (group): Convince traders/guards to leave behind 50–150 gp worth of nails, rope, lamp oil, or dried fodder. Success: Spire gains “Fortified +1” on its next defense/skill challenge.
Mount Readiness — Animal Handling DC 13 (group) or Leatherworker/Smith’s Tools DC 12: Fit tack, swap bad straps; bank Advantage on the party’s first Downdraft hazard during the Red Larch flight.
Security Sweep — Investigation or Insight DC 13: Check for sabotage, loose doors, or seditious murmurs. Success: avoid a later “strap-snap” complication at the Spire.
Route Marking — Survival or Cartographer’s Tools DC 12: Plot safe hop points to Red Larch. Success: party gains +2 to avoid the first travel encounter this leg.

text.h: Options & Consequences (pick what fits table choices)

list.li: Party escorts traders now: safer convoy; arrival a bit slower but with merchant goodwill (advantage on one Persuasion with caravans in Red Larch).
Party departs ahead, light and fast: earlier arrival; roll one extra weather/sky check en route.
Leave the prisoner here vs. take along:
Here: easier travel; later you may run a prisoner transfer complication.
With party: adds tension in the air; once en route, a DC 12 Persuasion/Intimidation can squeeze one more vague hint (“the champion hunts victories”).

text.h: Options & Consequences (pick what fits table choices)

list.li: Party escorts traders now: safer convoy; arrival a bit slower but with merchant goodwill (advantage on one Persuasion with caravans in Red Larch).
Party departs ahead, light and fast: earlier arrival; roll one extra weather/sky check en route.
Leave the prisoner here vs. take along:
Here: easier travel; later you may run a prisoner transfer complication.
With party: adds tension in the air; once en route, a DC 12 Persuasion/Intimidation can squeeze one more vague hint (“the champion hunts victories”).

text.h: Scene V — Return Flight to Red Larch (35–55 min)
text.p: Travel Note: Hippogriffs are reliable but not swift long-range flyers; treat pace as steady but susceptible to weather and carrying load. Plan short hops with rest points.
Sky Events (roll 1d6 or pick 2)

list.li: Mountain Downdraft (Group Dex (Acrobatics) or Wis (Animal Handling) DC 14): On fail, a rider descends; lose 30–60 minutes and make a DC 10 Con save vs. exhaustion for that mount.
Lingering Sky-Cult Scout (Encounter CR ~ party level −1): Chance to parley or rout; capture yields intel advantage in a later social scene.
Storm Line: Choice—land and wait (safe, +time) or press through (Con saves DC 12 vs. fatigue; Disadvantage on Perception for 1 hour).
Stranded Fledgling: Rescue grants goodwill with Savra (+1 future favor) and a modest gift at Red Larch.
Caravan Sighting: Offer of paid escort (small side payout, rumor seed).
Clear Skies: Make time; arrive earlier, refreshing vignette.

text.h: Scene VI — Red Larch Arrival (30–45 min)
text.p: Debrief with Harburk & Town Elders: Report on Aerisi; set the public tone (“Spire secured; valley safer”).
Ember Lances’ Turn-In: If they returned, they begin recruitment; if they stayed, Harburk asks the PCs to carry letters and funds back to Savra.
Downtime Options (pick 1–2 per PC): Craft, research cult symbols, train with locals, reputational boons.
Earth Tremors Near Sacred Stone Monastery (earth-cult pressure rises).
Vanishing Teamsters on the Long Road (perfect Skyrider/escort crossover).
Talos-Storm Signs returning in the hills (your earlier thread).

list.li: A courier from the Spire arrives with a wax-sealed charter for the New Skyriders—PCs listed as Founding Patrons.
A quiet moment at Rella’s marker in Red Larch; each PC may speak one line and gain Inspiration.

id-00085.name: Episode#3.00.00 Whispers at the Stone Bridge

text.p: Scene 1
text.frame: The air hangs heavy with chill moisture atop Feathergale Spire. The sky has remained overcast for days, the sun reduced to a pale smear behind rolling gray clouds. A low wind moans through the upper corridors, rattling loose panes and tugging at the banners until their edges fray. The horizon northward glows faintly gold at dawn, veiled by a long line of mist that snakes across the Sumber Hills like a living thing. The Spire hums with quiet activity. Savra Belabranta oversees the stables, her hair bound in a tight braid as she speaks with the riders who remain loyal. Her brother, Eren Belabranta, moves about the courtyard, still uneasy after the air cult’s collapse, trying to rebuild some semblance of order and trust. The party gathers in the mess hall — heavy oak tables, sunlight filtered to a dim gray through tall windows, dust motes drifting in the murk. It smells faintly of oil, parchment, and roasted barley.
text.p: Savra leans forward, her tone low and measured:
text.frame: “If you’re bound north, beware the road near the Stone Bridge. The knights who patrolled there returned shaken. They said the hills swallowed their voices — no echo, no sound at all. And one… swore he heard his own name whispered back.” She hesitates, her hand tightening around a mug. “That part I almost believe. The bridge has always had a strange quiet, but this… feels wrong.”
text.p: Eren Belabranta adds from across the room, voice heavy with fatigue:
text.frame: “There’s more. A merchant caravan was found just south of the bridge. Empty. Horses still tethered, carts upright — but not a soul around. The livestock in the nearby pasture were found dead the next morning. Eyes clouded, bodies twisted. Shepherds call it a blight.” He looks towards the party. “If there’s rot in the hills, it’s spreading.”
text.p: One of the Skywarden guards, a young man trying to sound brave, cuts in nervously:
text.frame: “I rode patrol near there three nights past. Couldn’t hear the wind — just this humming, soft and even, like someone was breathing behind me. I thought it was one of the others. But when I turned, they were all a good twenty paces away.” He swallows hard. “When I stopped, so did the hum.”
text.p: Finally, a passing courier warming himself by the brazier joins in, shaking his head:
text.frame: “They say the silence hunts sound now. Speak too loud near the bridge, and it follows you home. I’d stay clear of that place if I were you.”
text.p: From here, the party may:

list.li: Question Savra or Eren (Investigation / Insight DC 13): Learn that the odor of decay was first reported from a cave near the bridge, not the bridge itself.
Ask about the missing caravan (Investigation DC 15): Eren provides a torn parchment seal bearing a faded sigil — a necromantic rune half-burned away.
Speak with the guard (Persuasion DC 12): He mentions seeing faint blue fire flicker briefly over the hill at night, “like a lantern under the soil.”

text.p: As the rumors settle, a gust sweeps through the open window, carrying the faint scent of wet soil and rot from the north.
For a moment, even within the stone walls of the Spire, all noise falls away — the flag banners hang still, and only the party’s breath fills the silence.
Then the wind resumes, and the uneasy calm is broken.
Savra turns to the group:
text.frame: “If you truly mean to seek out the Scarlet Moon Tower, you’ll have to pass near that bridge. Perhaps… best to uncover what’s festering there first. Whatever it is, it’s not natural.”
text.p: Setting
text.frame: The morning the party departs ****, the sky hangs low and bruised, streaked with dim light that never quite breaks through the clouds. The air feels damp and metallic. Wind rattles the Spire's high banners as the gates creak open. The faint scent of rain and stone lingers as the group readies their mounts and gear, preparing to ride north toward the Stone Bridge. The courtyard, usually alive with motion, has fallen still. Footsteps echo sharply on wet flagstones. It is in this uneasy quiet that the **Emberlances** appear—a small band of armored riders led by **Captain Dareth Holt**. Their crimson cloaks are darkened with moisture, their expressions drawn and hollow.

The Emberlances dismount, their boots splashing into the thin puddles scattered across the courtyard. Brighthammer removes his helm and holds it under his arm, his eyes weary but resolute. "Before you depart," he says quietly, glancing at each of you in turn, "you should know—someone or *something* has disturbed **Rella Sunspur’s** grave." He waits a moment, as if expecting disbelief. "It happened last night, we think. The soil was torn open from within. No tracks, no signs of shovels or tools. The earth looked... wrong. Like it had rotted in a single night."

One of the younger Emberlances, eyes red from lack of sleep, speaks up. "Her grave marker was shattered. We found bits of her cloak—the one she wore on the last mission—but the body’s gone. The ground around it—the grass was black. Dead."
Another adds, voice tight, "The priests say they didn’t sense any necromancy in the area yesterday. Whatever did this… it came fast, and it left nothing behind."
Brighthammer’s jaw clenches. "We sealed the ground again, out of respect. But I had to tell you before you left. You fought beside her. She deserves at least that truth."
text.p: The party can respond in several ways:
* **Investigation / Insight (DC 13):** Determine that the Emberlances are genuinely shaken—not from fear, but from guilt and confusion. They suspect desecration but fear to name it.
* **Religion / Arcana (DC 15):** The description of the decay suggests **unnatural reanimation** or a **spirit forcibly displaced** rather than traditional necromancy.

* **Persuasion / Intimidation (DC 12):** Convince Holt to let them examine the grave themselves. He hesitates but will agree if pressed, warning: "If you go, tread light. The ground itself feels... watchful."
A low rumble of distant thunder rolls across the hills as the Emberlances remount. Before leaving, Holt pauses, his gaze heavy on the party.
> "If you find who or what did this," he says, voice steady but low, "make sure she rests again. She earned that much."
As their hooves fade into the mist, the wind rises, carrying a faint odor of decay from the north—the same direction the party is bound.
Setting

The trail north from **Skywarden Spire** winds through low, wind-swept hills before dropping into a shallow valley dotted with a few stubborn farms. By the time the party arrives, the day has turned gray and wet, drizzle clinging to cloaks and armor. A thick, unnatural stillness blankets the fields—no bird calls, no insects, only the hiss of wind through blackened grass.

A lone farmstead comes into view: a sagging barn, its red paint stripped to dull wood, and a small farmhouse with boarded windows. A half-collapsed fence leans around a pasture where the soil looks churned and sickly. The smell hits first—**a foul blend of rot, iron, and wet hay**.
When the party approaches, they find **signs of struggle**:
* A **wagon wheel**, half-buried in mud, spattered with old blood.
* Several **dead sheep**, their bodies twisted and gray, flesh sunken as though drained.
* A **trail of blackened footprints** (DC 13 Survival) leading from the barn to a nearby irrigation ditch.
> A faint hum drifts through the air, so low it’s felt more than heard—like the ground itself is vibrating. When the wind stills, it stops.
### Searching the Barn
The barn door hangs open, one hinge shrieking softly in the wind. Inside:
* Tools scattered across the floor, a pitchfork driven deep into a support beam.
* Strange **sigils drawn in ash** (DC 15 Arcana/Religion) — symbols of **preservation magic twisted into decay**, evidence of experimentation.
* A **dead farmhand** slumped near the hayloft ladder, his eyes black and pupils dilated to pinpoints. His expression is peaceful—too peaceful.
If examined, a **DC 14 Medicine check** reveals:
> The man died within the last day, but the **decay is advanced**, skin bloated and splitting as though weeks have passed.

linklist.link: Encounter: Episode#3.00.00 Whispers at the Stone Bridge

text.p: As the party inspects the barn, the low hum returns—this time from beneath the floor. The planks shudder, and with a sudden crack, **two Hollowed Farmhands** claw their way up through the dirt, their mouths gaping wide, emitting a droning resonance that numbs the air
Combat should be brief and eerie—thick with sound and silence. The creatures crumble into **ashen soil** when slain, leaving behind faint traces of gray dust that hum faintly if disturbed.
### Clues & Leads
When the fight ends, the barn quiets completely. Searching the area yields:
* **Torn parchment** with a charcoal sketch of a stone outcropping marked with a rune (DC 12 Investigation).
Skogul or Hector can recognize it as a depiction of **Lance Rock**, a few miles north.
* **Broken holy charm** of Kelemvor, smeared with mud—likely belonging to one of the missing caravan guards mentioned earlier.

> The air grows colder as the party steps outside. Crows circle far above, silent. Beyond the northern ridge, the faint silhouette of **Lance Rock** juts up like a black tooth against the storming sky.
### Transition

The party now has a clear lead pointing them toward **Lance Rock**, where the truth behind the blight and Rella’s disturbed grave awaits. As they depart the ruined farm, a final gust of wind carries the smell of rot and iron—then fades, leaving only the oppressive quiet of the hills.

description.p: Dark green stone
Jade,

Tonight is a small, private scavenger hunt made just for us—quiet, simple, and ours alone—with clues that represent my principles of love. It takes place in our home at 11422 Kingsbarn Court, Tomball, Texas 77377. Each step is a little memory and a promise about the life we’re building.

Your sun warms my bones, your moon keeps my soul, and your stars teach my thoughts where to go. Banner high, oath kept: I choose you, respect you, lead with kindness, and walk this map with you forever.
First clue → Please start at your desk.
Behind the framed photo of us—the one tied to our song “Here to Mars” by Coheed and Cambria—you’ll find the next note.
With all my love,
Thomas

Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of a freedom of movement spell for 8 hours.

The Potion Bandolier is a specialized wearable item designed to hold and quickly deliver alchemical potions in combat. Crafted from reinforced leather with enchanted clasps and glass-cradle stitching, the bandolier enables the wearer to use potions with increased efficiency while adding a layer of strategic limitation. It becomes more powerful as the character gains experience, unlocking more storage and customization through feats.
• Potions stored in the bandolier can be used as a bonus action (1 per turn).
• Potions must be pre-loaded into the bandolier to be used this way.
• A character may only use one bandolier potion per turn, regardless of other effects.
• Reloading a potion into the bandolier takes 1 action per potion in combat.
• Reloading outside of combat takes 1 minute for the full bandolier.
• If the wearer is hit by a critical hit or rolls a natural 1 on a saving throw, they must roll a d20 (DC 10).
• On failure, a random potion stored in the bandolier breaks and is lost (no effect occurs).
• Some feats mitigate or interact with this rule.
Players may swap one of their bandolier feats for another feat of equal or lower tier during downtime.
The cost is based on the tier of the new feat being chosen.
• Players may not select feats above their current bandolier tier.
• Respecs must be performed during downtime with appropriate tools or facilities.

description.p: Occasionally your experiments go awry. You’ve learned to harness this ability in the form of explosives. Upon completing a long rest, an alchemist can create a number of explosives equal to their Intelligence modifier plus profencies bonus (minimum of 1). These explosives can be thrown as an action to a range of 20ft. and deal 1d8 fire damage to a target it comes into contact with, at 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8). Use your strength modifier for the attack roll. All creatures within 5ft. of the impacted target are subject to the explosive’s splash damage and must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take fire damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). All prepared explosives become inert as soon as you complete your next long rest. You need alchemy supplies to prepare explosives. Your discoveries may allow you to create special explosives; This will require to exchange set amount which depends on the discovery you have chosen.

description.p: By decree of Lord Protector Dagult Neverember, rightful authority over Sword Coast North — Phandalin Region, the bearer(s) Sethari, Rhi’Knivir, Edrin Callen, Lyra Shadefoot, and Vorgrim are granted full pardon for all offenses within Sword Coast North — Phandalin Region, excluding murder. Officers are commanded to cease pursuit and release the bearer(s) for qualifying offenses and record such clemency. Valid only within Sword Coast North — Phandalin Region. Seal: Indigo wax impressed with the Lord Protector’s signet (Great Seal of Neverwinter), bound with black-and-silver ribbon. Registry: NW-CLM-1492-0912. Date: 12 Marpenoth, 1492 DR.

id-00015.name: Writ of Pardon under the Seal of [Sword Coast North]

description.p: Do not kill the dwarf unless you must. Catch him. Take what he carries. Any map goes to the castle at once.

id-00017.name: Crude Written Order
id-00017.nonidentified: A stained scrap of parchment covered in rough, bossy handwriting.

description.p: Soot-dark ridged wax with gray flecks; one end flattened from use. Faint smoke-tallow scent; hardens unusually fast—typical of traveling censors.

dm_privatenotes.p: Forensic linker that stitches prior scenes (Inn blotter, etc.) to the granary; lowers friction on “same forger” reveals.

description.p: Ruled page logging dates, payers, purposes; escort fees align with recent ordeal nights. Margin note (same hand): “Patrol coverage assured on noted nights.” Grain dust lingers in the fold.

dm_privatenotes.p: Clean collusion proof and a tool to peel mercenaries off (“off-contract”); approving initials double as a future lead.

id-00078.name: Ledger Page — Escort Fees vs. Ordeal Nights

description.p: A polished vessel of brass and crystal, etched with tiny rings that drift like constellations beneath its surface. When held close, the vessel gives off a faint warmth, as though something inside is breathing in a quiet dream. Its seamless shell opens not by hand, but by will, answering only to the creature that has bound itself to its magic.
While attuned to this item, you can bind one willing creature to the vessel. The vessel can store only one creature at a time.
As an action, you can throw the vessel to a point you can see within 30 feet and release the bound creature. The creature appears in the vessel’s space or the nearest unoccupied space.
As an action, while the bound creature is within 5 feet of you, you can store it back inside the vessel. The creature must be willing.
The vessel can hold only one creature at a time. If a creature is already stored within it, no other creature can be bound or stored in the vessel.
A stored creature remains in magical stasis inside the vessel. Time passes normally for it, and it emerges with the same hit points, conditions, and ongoing effects it had when it was stored.
If your attunement to the vessel ends while a creature is stored inside, that creature immediately appears in the nearest unoccupied space.

A small vial pendant on a bronze chain, framed in copper and stained faint blue-green from old alchemical residue. The clasp is practical, reinforced for travel, and the glass is scratched from years of wear. One side of the metal cap is polished smooth where Elenya’s thumb used to rest when she was thinking.

id-00082.name: Elenya’s necklace
id-00082.nonidentified: Bronze necklace with a small glass vial pendant stained by old blue-green alchemical residue. Reinforced clasp, currently broken.

description.p: Just a small keg of drink—mainly a trade good or gift
Look/Smell: Translucent, veined bladder filled with green, syrupy acid; sharp vinegar-metal scent.

linklist.link: Handling: Keep tied off and wrapped in oilcloth, inside a rigid, stoppered glass or wax-sealed container. Keep upright; avoid iron and reactive metals. Chalk/wood ash will neutralize small spills.

list.li: Glass bottle: 2 gp
Candle (for wax seal): 1 cp
Small sack (padding): 1 cp

description.p: Total: 2 gp, 2 cp

Use (common): Sold to apothecaries or herbalists for etching/solvent work; can be distilled into a standard vial of acid (PHB) by someone with alchemist’s supplies and a workspace (Adabra could do this in town).
Shelf life: Best within a few days; lasts about a tenday if kept cool and sealed. Preservatives (strong alcohol/salt) extend life.

A translucent, veined sac of syrupy green acid sealed inside a rigid glass bottle with a waxed cork and padded in cloth. The air-tight seal slows decay; kept cool and upright, it stays viable for about one tenday. Alchemists can refine this into 1 vial of acid (PHB) with alchemist’s supplies and a workspace. Handle gently—avoid metal contact; chalk or wood ash will neutralize small spills.
Harvest: Wis (Survival) DC 12, 10 minutes → 2d10 intact spikes
A dense, foot-long barb from a manticore’s tail, ridged with backward micro-hooks. Wrapped at the base, it throws true and punches deep before the barbs snag and twist, ruining the spike for reuse.
Distilled from a manticore’s reflective eye. The liquid holds a faint green sheen; a single dose smears the pupil and sharpens low-light contrast.
Harvest: Wis (Survival) DC 11, 5 minutes (use within 24h unless preserved)
Effect: For 1 hour, gain darkvision 60 ft (or +30 ft if you already have darkvision). Does not stack with itself.

Axebeaks possess extremely dense, mineral-rich keratin in their beaks. When properly harvested and processed, parts of the creature can be used in weapon maintenance, alchemy, and minor martial enhancements.
Uses
Sharpen Axes: For 24 hours, an axe (handaxe/battleaxe/greataxe) deals +1 damage on the first hit per combat and has advantage on checks to chop/breach wood. Doesn’t stack with magic weapons.
Track Beasts (keratin): Advantage on one Survival check to track beasts (1 hour).
Anti-Disarm (sinew): Advantage on the first check to resist being disarmed.
A corrupted javelin made from driftwood and bone, soaked in polluted water and rot.
If the target fails a DC 12 Constitution save, they are Poisoned until the end of their next turn (from infection or rot).
A rough-hewn javelin of warped wood and chipped iron, bound together with sinew, scrap leather, and whatever else the goblins could steal or strip from the dead.
The target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failure the target is poisoned for 1 hour.
On a failure by 5 or more, the target is poisoned for 1 day The target wakes up if it takes damage or if another creature takes an action to shake it awake.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d6 Acid damage.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist's Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 1d4 Fire damage and start burning (see the rules glossary).

This musical instrument has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While you are playing it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and write a magical message on a nonmagical object or surface that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The message can be up to six words long and is written in a language you know. If you are a Bard, you can scribe an additional seven words and make the message glow faintly, allowing it to be seen in nonmagical Darkness. Casting the Dispel Magic spell on the message erases it. Otherwise, the message fades away after 24 hours.

As a Utilize action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a Net. Target a creature you can see within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or have the Restrained condition until it escapes. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. Destroying the Net (AC 10; 5 HP; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage) also frees the target, ending the effect.
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra 5 Fire damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the Utilize action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn't need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a Utilize action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.

description.p: This sticky black unguent is thick and heavy in the container, but it flows quickly when poured. The oil can cover a Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it's wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium).
Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of a freedom of movement spell for 8 hours.
Alternatively, the oil can be poured on the ground as an action, where it covers a 10-foot square, duplicating the effect of the grease spell in that area for 8 hours.

id-00002.name: Flask of Grease
id-00002.nonidentified: This flask contains a thick and heavy black unguent which is sticky to the touch.

description.p: One vial of this oil can cover one Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it's wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of the Freedom of Movement spell for 8 hours.
Alternatively, the oil can be poured on the ground as a Magic action, where it covers a 10-foot square, duplicating the effect of the Grease spell in that area for 8 hours.
This sticky, black unguent is thick and heavy, but it flows quickly when poured.

id-00003.name: Oil of Slipperiness
id-00003.nonidentified: A vial full of sticky, black unguent.

description.p: When you drink this potion, you have Resistance to psychic damage for 1 hour.

id-00004.nonidentified: The liquid in this potion has an orange tinge to it.

id-00005.name: Potion of Healing (Good)
id-00005.nonidentified: The potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

description.p: When you drink this potion, you have Resistance to force damage for 1 hour.

id-00006.name: Potion of Force Resistance
id-00006.nonidentified: The liquid in this potion has a brown tinge to it.

description.p: You regain 2d4 + 2 hit points when you drink this potion. The potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

id-00007.name: Potion of Healing

id-00008.name: Potion of Healing (Potent)
id-00008.nonidentified: The potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

description.p: This concoction looks, smells, and tastes like a Potion of Healing or another beneficial potion. However, it is actually poison masked by illusion magic. Identify reveals its true nature.
If you drink this potion, you take 4d6 Poison damage and must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

id-00009.name: Potion of Poison
id-00009.nonidentified: This concoction looks, smells, and tastes like a Potion of Healing

description.p: When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the Comprehend Languages spell for 1 hour.
This potion's liquid is a clear concoction with bits of salt and soot swirling in it.

id-00010.name: Potion of Comprehension
id-00010.nonidentified: This potion's liquid is a clear concoction with bits of salt and soot swirling in it.

description.p: When you drink this potion, your Strength score changes to 25 for 1 hour. The potion has no effect on you if your Strength is equal to or greater than that score.
This potion's transparent liquid has floating in it a sliver of light resembling a giant's fingernail.

id-00011.nonidentified: This potion's transparent liquid has floating in it a sliver of light resembling a giant's fingernail.

description.p: You regain 5d4 + 5Hit Points when you drink this potion.

description.p: After you drink this potion, each Unarmed Strike you make deals an extra 1d6 Force damage on a hit. This effect lasts 10 minutes.

id-00013.name: Potion of Pugilism
id-00013.nonidentified: This potion is a thick green fluid that tastes like spinach.

description.p: You regain d4 + 1 hit points when you drink this potion. The potion's red liquid glimmers when agitated.

description.p: When you drink this potion, you can cast the level 3 version of the Animal Friendship spell (save DC 13).

id-00016.name: Potion of Animal Friendship
id-00016.nonidentified: A vial containing a muddy liquid.

description.p: This bottle contains a breath of elemental air. When you inhale it, you either exhale it or hold it.

If you exhale the breath, you gain the effect of the gust of wind spell. If you hold the breath, you don't need to breathe for 1 hour, though you can end this benefit early (for example, to speak). Ending it early doesn't give you the benefit of exhaling the breath.

id-00017.name: Bottled Breath
id-00017.nonidentified: This bottle, although stoppered, appears to be empty

description.p: When you drink this potion, your Strength score changes for 1 hour. The type of giant determines the score (see the table below). The potion has no effect on you if your Strength is equal to or greater than that score.

id-00018.nonidentified: This potion's transparent liquid has floating in it a sliver of light resembling a giant's fingernail.

id-00019.nonidentified: The liquid in this potion has a dark tinge to it.

description.p: When you drink this potion, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed for 1 hour. During this time, you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks you make to climb. The potion is separated into brown, silver, and gray layers resembling bands of stone. Shaking the bottle fails to mix the colors.
Drinking or administering a potion takes an action.

id-00020.name: Potion of Climbing
id-00020.nonidentified: The three liquids in this vial are separated into three layers colored brown, silver and gray respectively.

description.p: This spell scroll bears the words of a single spell, Ray of Frost , written in a mystical cipher. If the spell is on your class's spell list, you can read the scroll and cast its spell without providing any material components. Otherwise, the scroll is unintelligible. Casting the spell by reading the scroll requires the spell's normal casting time. Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and it crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll is not lost.

If the spell is on your class's spell list but of a higher level than you can normally cast, you must make an ability check using your spellcasting ability to determine whether you cast it successfully. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a failed check, the spell disappears from the scroll with no other effect.
Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and the scroll itself crumbles to dust.
This spell scroll's saving throw DC 13 and attack bonus +5.

A wizard spell on a spell scroll can be copied just as spells in spellbooks can be copied. When a spell is copied from a spell scroll , the copier must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check with a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. If the check succeeds, the spell is successfully copied. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the spell scroll is destroyed.

If the spell is on your class's spell list, you can read the scroll and cast its spell without providing any material components. Otherwise, the scroll is unintelligible. Casting the spell by reading the scroll requires the spell's normal casting time. Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and it crumbles to dust. If the casting is interrupted, the scroll is not lost.

If the spell is on your class's spell list but of a higher level than you can normally cast, you must make an ability check using your spellcasting ability to determine whether you cast it successfully. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a failed check, the spell disappears from the scroll with no other effect.
Once the spell is cast, the words on the scroll fade, and the scroll itself crumbles to dust.
This spell scroll's saving throw DC 15 and attack bonus +7.

A wizard spell on a spell scroll can be copied just as spells in spellbooks can be copied. When a spell is copied from a spell scroll , the copier must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check with a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. If the check succeeds, the spell is successfully copied. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the spell scroll is destroyed.

description.p: This suit of armor is reinforced with adamantine, one of the hardest substances in existence. While you're wearing it, any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit.

Of all the armor categories, heavy armor offers the best protection. These suits of armor cover the entire body and are designed to stop a wide range of attacks. Only proficient warriors can manage their weight and bulk.

Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor. Buckles and straps distribute the weight over the body.

id-00001.name: Adamantine Plate Armor
id-00001.nonidentified: This suit of armor is reinforced with a strange metal.

description.p: Mithral is a light, flexible metal. A mithral chain shirt or breastplate can be worn under normal clothes. If the armor normally imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks or has a Strength requirement, the mithral version of the armor doesn't.

Of all the armor categories, heavy armor offers the best protection. These suits of armor cover the entire body and are designed to stop a wide range of attacks. Only proficient warriors can manage their weight and bulk.
This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible chain mail protects the joints.

id-00002.name: Mithral Splint Armor
id-00002.nonidentified: This armor has been made with an extremely light and flexible metal.

description.p: While wearing this armor, you have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. In addition, whenever you start your turn underwater with 0 hit points, the armor causes you to rise 60 feet toward the surface. The armor is decorated with fish and shell motifs.

Medium armor offers more protection than light armor, but it also impairs movement more. If you wear medium armor, you add your Dexterity modifier, to a maximum of +2, to the base number from your armor type to determine your Armor Class.

Made of interlocking metal rings, a chain shirt is worn between layers of clothing or leather. This armor offers modest protection to the wearer's upper body and allows the sound of the rings rubbing against one another to be muffled by outer layers.

description.p: These furred boots are snug and feel quite warm. While you wear them, you gain the following benefits:

list.li: You have resistance to cold damage.
You ignore difficult terrain created by ice or snow.
You can tolerate temperatures as low as -50 degrees Fahrenheit without any additional protection. If you wear heavy clothes, you can tolerate temperatures as low as -100 degrees Fahrenheit.

id-00002.name: Boots of the Winterlands
id-00002.nonidentified: Made of fine leather and lined with the softest of furs these knee length boots look very comfortable and warm.

description.p: While wearing this cloak with its hood up, you can breathe underwater, and you have a swimming speed of 60 feet. Pulling the hood up or down requires an action.

id-00003.name: Cloak of the Manta Ray
id-00003.nonidentified: This cloak has been woven from really fine material embroidered with gold thread. It has a strange tail-like appendage on its back hem.

description.p: This stoppered flask sloshes when shaken, as if it contains water. The decanter weighs 2 pounds.

You can use an action to remove the stopper and speak one of three command words, whereupon an amount of fresh water or salt water (your choice) pours out of the flask. The water stops pouring out at the start of your next turn. Choose from the following options:

list.li: "Stream" produces 1 gallon of water.
"Fountain" produces 5 gallons of water.

"Geyser" produces 30 gallons of water that gushes forth in a geyser 30 feet long and 1 foot wide. As a bonus action while holding the decanter, you can aim the geyser at a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or take 1d4 bludgeoning damage and fall prone. Instead of a creature, you can target an object that isn't being worn or carried and that weighs no more than 200 pounds. The object is either knocked over or pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

id-00004.name: Decanter of Endless Water
id-00004.nonidentified: This stoppered flask sloshes when shaken as if it contains water.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d6 Acid damage.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist's Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 1d4 Fire damage and start burning (see the rules glossary).
As a Bonus Action, you can drink a vial of Antitoxin to gain Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

As a Utilize action, you can spill Ball Bearings from their pouch. They spread to cover a level, 10-foot-square area within 10 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Ball Bearings.
A Barrel holds up to 40 gallons of liquid or up to 4 cubic feet of dry goods.
A Basket holds up to 40 pounds within 2 cubic feet.
A Bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. While in a Bedroll, you automatically succeed on saving throws against extreme cold (see the Dungeon Master's Guide).
When rung as a Utilize action, a Bell produces a sound that can be heard up to 60 feet away.
While wrapped in a blanket, you have Advantage on saving throws against extreme cold (see the Dungeon Master's Guide).
A Block and Tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

A Book contains fiction or nonfiction. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks you make about that topic.
A Glass Bottle holds up to 11/2 pints.
A Bucket holds up to half a cubic foot of contents.

As a Utilize action, you can spread Caltrops from their bag to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. A creature that enters this area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. It takes 10 minutes to recover the Caltrops.
For 1 hour, a lit Candle sheds Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 5 feet.
A Crossbow Bolt Case holds up to 20 Bolts.
A Map or Scroll Case holds up to 10 sheets of paper or 5 sheets of parchment.

As a Utilize action, you can wrap a Chain around an unwilling creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Chain requires the creature to make a successful DC 18 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action. Bursting the Chain requires a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.
A Chest holds up to 12 cubic feet of contents.

A Climber's Kit includes boot tips, gloves, pitons, and a harness. As a Utilize action, you can use the Climber's Kit to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the anchor point, and you can't move more than 25 feet from there without undoing the anchor as a Bonus Action.
Fine Clothes are made of expensive fabrics and adorned with expertly crafted details. Some events and locations admit only people wearing these clothes.
Traveler's Clothes are resilient garments designed for travel in various environments.
A Component Pouch is watertight and filled with compartments that hold all the free Material components of your spells.
While wearing a Costume, you have Advantage on any ability check you make to impersonate the person or type of person it represents.
Using a Crowbar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Crowbar's leverage can be applied.
A Flask holds up to 1 pint.

As a Utilize action, you can throw the Grappling Hook at a railing, a ledge, or another catch within 50 feet of yourself, and the hook catches on if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. If you tied a Rope to the hook, you can then climb it.
A Healer's Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Holy Water. Target one creature you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 Radiant damage if it is a Fiend or an Undead.

As a Utilize action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 Piercing damage and have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 Piercing damage to the trapped creature.
A Jug holds up to 1 gallon.
A Ladder is 10 feet tall. You must climb to move up or down it.
A Lamp burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet.
A Bullseye Lantern burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet.

A Hooded Lantern burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, or raise it again.
A Lock comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use Thieves' Tools to pick this Lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.

As a Utilize action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. While bound, a creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls, and the creature is Restrained if the Manacles are attached to a chain or hook that is fixed in place. Escaping the Manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check as an action. Bursting them requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check as an action.
Each set of Manacles comes with a key. Without the key, a creature can use Thieves' Tools to pick the Manacles' lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.
A handheld steel Mirror is useful for personal cosmetics but also for peeking around corners and reflecting light as a signal.

When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a Net. Target a creature you can see within 15 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or have the Restrained condition until it escapes. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. Destroying the Net (AC 10; 5 HP; Immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage) also frees the target, ending the effect.
You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra 5 Fire damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the Utilize action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn't need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a Utilize action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.

A Magnifying Glass grants Advantage on any ability check made to appraise or inspect a highly detailed item. Lighting a fire with a Magnifying Glass requires light as bright as sunlight to focus, tinder to ignite, and about 5 minutes for the fire to ignite.
If you consult an accurate Map, you gain a +5 bonus to Wisdom (Survival) checks you make to find your way in the place represented on it.
One sheet of Paper can hold about 250 handwritten words.
One sheet of Parchment can hold about 250 handwritten words.
Perfume comes in a 4-ounce vial. For 1 hour after applying Perfume to yourself, you have Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks made to influence an Indifferent Humanoid within 5 feet of yourself.

As a Bonus Action, you can use a vial of Basic Poison to coat one weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. A creature that takes Piercing or Slashing damage from the poisoned weapon or ammunition takes an extra 1d4 Poison damage. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute or until its damage is dealt, whichever comes first.

A Pole is 10 feet long. You can use it to touch something up to 10 feet away. If you must make a Strength (Athletics) check as part of a High or Long Jump, you can use the Pole to vault, giving yourself Advantage on the check.
An Iron Pot holds up to 1 gallon.
A Pouch holds up to 6 pounds within one-fifth of a cubic foot.
A Quiver holds up to 20 Arrows.
You can use a Portable Ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus to the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you Advantage on this check.
Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See "Malnutrition" in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.
A Robe has vocational or ceremonial significance. Some events and locations admit only people wearing a Robe bearing certain colors or symbols.
As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition. If the creature's legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.
A Sack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot.
Working for 1 hour, you can use a Shovel to dig a hole that is 5 feet on each side in soil or similar material.
When blown as a Utilize action, a Signal Whistle produces a sound that can be heard up to 600 feet away.

A Book contains fiction or nonfiction. If you consult an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic, you gain a +5 bonus to Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks you make about that topic.

As a Utilize action, you can use a blunt object, such as a Light Hammer, to hammer a spike into wood, earth, or a similar material. You can do so to jam a door shut or to then tie a Rope or Chain to the Spike.

Iron Spikes come in bundles of ten. As a Utilize action, you can use a blunt object, such as a Light Hammer, to hammer a spike into wood, earth, or a similar material. You can do so to jam a door shut or to then tie a Rope or Chain to the Spike.
Objects viewed through a Spyglass are magnified to twice their size.
String is 10 feet long. You can tie a knot in it as a Utilize action.
A Tent sleeps up to two Small or Medium creatures.

A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a Candle, Lamp, Lantern, or Torch-or anything else with exposed fuel-takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.
A Vial holds up to 4 ounces.
A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don't drink sufficient water, you risk dehydration (see the rules glossary).

A Spell Scroll (Cantrip) is a magic item that bears the words of a cantrip determined by the scroll's creator. If the spell is on your class's spell list, you can read the scroll and cast the spell using its normal casting time and without providing any Material components.
If the spell requires a saving throw or an attack roll, the spell save DC is 13, and the attack bonus is +5. The scroll disintegrates when the casting is completed.

A Spell Scroll (Level 1) is a magic item that bears the words of a level 1 spell, determined by the scroll's creator. If the spell is on your class's spell list, you can read the scroll and cast the spell using its normal casting time and without providing any Material components.
If the spell requires a saving throw or an attack roll, the spell save DC is 13, and the attack bonus is +5. The scroll disintegrates when the casting is completed.
Magic weapons are unmistakably finer in quality than their ordinary counterparts. You have a +1 bonus to the attack rolls and damage rolls you make with this weapon.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Curse. This sword is cursed and possessed by a vengeful spirit. Becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the sword, keeping it on your person at all times. While attuned to this weapon, you have disadvantage on attack rolls made with weapons other than this one.

In addition, while the sword is on your person, you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw whenever you take damage in combat. On a failed save, you must attack the creature that damaged you until you drop to 0 hit points or it does, or until you can't reach the creature to make a melee attack against it.
You can break the curse in the usual ways. Alternatively, casting banishment on the sword forces the vengeful spirit to leave it. The sword then becomes a +1 weapon with no other properties.

id-00005.nonidentified: This weapon was not made by some second class craftsman that's for sure. There are a number of delicate runes along the blade and several semi-precious gems are inlaid into the guard.
